observations.title: sdd/neon-dash/explore
Neon Dash — one-button browser arcade game proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Neon Dash

## Intent

Build a one-button browser arcade game that is instantly playable, visually striking, and addictive through a tight core loop: tap to dash through obstacles, survive as long as possible, beat your high score. Zero dependencies, zero friction — open an HTML file and play.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Core game loop: menu → playing → dead → menu (3-state machine)
- One-tap dash mechanic with ~80ms invincibility window
- Pattern-based obstacle spawning (learnable, not pure random)
- Exponential difficulty curve (speed + gap shrink over time)
- Score + multiplier chains (combo resets on death)
- Best score persistence via localStorage
- Neon visual style: additive blending glow, particle bursts, screen shake on death
- Web Audio API sound effects (dash, death, score milestone)
- Input normalization: keyboard (Space/Enter) + touch
- Instant restart: tap to restart in <1 second
- Responsive canvas sizing for desktop and mobile

### Out of Scope
- Near-miss recognition / "Close call!" bonus (v2)
- Power-ups, levels, or multiple game modes
- Leaderboards or online scoring
- Music / background audio tracks
- Settings menu (volume, controls, etc.)
- Any external library, framework, or bundler

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `game-core`: Game loop, state machine, player physics, obstacle spawning, collision detection, scoring
- `neon-rendering`: Canvas rendering with additive blending glow, particles, screen shake, trail effects
- `audio-effects`: Web Audio API sound generation for game events
- `input-handling`: Keyboard and touch input normalization

### Modified Capabilities
- None

## Approach

**Architecture**: Single `requestAnimationFrame` loop with delta-time capping at 50ms. Semi-fixed timestep — no accumulator needed for simple AABB collision.

**Code structure**: 7 small files using IIFE modules on `window.NEON` namespace. No bundler, no ES modules, zero config.

**Neon rendering**: `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'` + concentric shapes for glow. NO `shadowBlur` (not GPU-accelerated). Pre-render static elements to offscreen canvas.

**Audio**: Lazy AudioContext on first user gesture. OscillatorNode + GainNode for short effects. Try/catch all localStorage and AudioContext calls.

**Performance**: Cap particles at 100 (50 on mobile), trail at 15 positions, 1-2 glow layers. Use `fillRect` not `arc` for particles.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `neon-dash/index.html` | New | Entry point, canvas, overlay containers (<50 lines) |
| `neon-dash/css/style.css` | New | Layout, overlays, responsive canvas sizing (<100 lines) |
| `neon-dash/js/main.js` | New | State machine, game loop, score/best-score management |
| `neon-dash/js/player.js` | New | Player class: position, dash, collision box, draw (~60 lines) |
| `neon-dash/js/obstacles.js` | New | ObstacleManager: spawn, move, pattern-based, AABB collision (~100 lines) |
| `neon-dash/js/render.js` | New | Pure render functions: background, game, overlay (~150 lines) |
| `neon-dash/js/particles.js` | New | ParticleSystem: emit, update, draw, cap at 100 (~80 lines) |
| `neon-dash/js/audio.js` | New | SoundManager: lazy AudioContext, oscillator effects (~100 lines) |
| `neon-dash/js/input.js` | New | Input module: keyboard + touch normalization (~60 lines) |
| `neon-dash/package.json` | New | Dev server script only |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| AudioContext autoplay policy breaks sound | Medium | Lazy init on first gesture, try/catch resume, mute toggle |
| Canvas performance on low-end mobile | Medium | Reduce particles to 50, trail to 8, glow to 1 layer on touch devices |
| dt spiral on tab switch | Low | Hard cap dt at 0.05s |
| Touch double-fire with keyboard | Low | 50ms input cooldown after dash |
| Scope creep | Medium | Ship core loop first, polish second, everything else is v2 |

## Rollback Plan

Delete the `neon-dash/` directory. No existing code is modified — this is a greenfield addition.

## Dependencies

- None. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS only. Optional: `npx serve` or `python3 -m http.server` for local dev.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Game opens in browser, shows menu screen with neon styling
- [ ] Tap/click/space starts the game, player dashes forward
- [ ] Obstacles spawn from right, move left, collision triggers death
- [ ] Score increases while alive, multiplier builds on consecutive dashes
- [ ] Death screen shows score + best score, tap restarts instantly
- [ ] Best score persists across page reloads (localStorage)
- [ ] Sound effects play on dash, death, and score milestones
- [ ] Particle bursts on death, screen shake on collision
- [ ] Runs at 60fps on desktop, 30+ fps on mobile
- [ ] No external dependencies, no build step, single HTML file opens and plays

observations.title: sdd/neon-dash/spec
observations.content:
# Neon Dash — Specification

## game-core

### Requirement: Game State Machine

The system MUST implement a 3-state finite state machine: `menu`, `playing`, `dead`. Transitions: `menu→playing` on first user input, `playing→dead` on collision, `dead→menu` after 1-second delay OR `dead→playing` on user input (instant restart).

#### Scenario: Start game from menu
- GIVEN the game is in `menu` state with the title screen visible
- WHEN the user presses Space, Enter, or taps the screen
- THEN the state transitions to `playing` and the game loop begins

#### Scenario: Player death transitions to dead state
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state
- WHEN the player collides with an obstacle
- THEN the state transitions to `dead`, death effects trigger, and input is locked for 500ms to prevent accidental restart

#### Scenario: Instant restart from dead state
- GIVEN the game is in `dead` state and 500ms have elapsed since death
- WHEN the user presses Space, Enter, or taps
- THEN the state transitions to `playing` with all game state reset

### Requirement: Game Loop Timing

The system MUST use `requestAnimationFrame` with delta-time calculation. Delta time MUST be capped at 50ms to prevent physics tunneling after tab switches. When in `menu` or `dead` state (after effects complete), the loop MUST NOT continue calling `requestAnimationFrame` to preserve battery.

#### Scenario: Normal frame timing
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state
- WHEN `requestAnimationFrame` fires with timestamp `t`
- THEN `dt = min((t - lastTime) / 1000, 0.05)` is computed and used for all updates

#### Scenario: Tab switch produces large dt
- GIVEN the game was running and the user switches tabs for 5 seconds
- WHEN the user returns and the next frame fires
- THEN `dt` is capped at 0.05, preventing the player from tunneling through obstacles

### Requirement: Player Physics and Dash

The player MUST have a fixed vertical lane position. The dash mechanic MUST move the player forward (right) with a short burst, then the player drifts back. The dash MUST grant ~80ms of invincibility frames. Dash MUST have a cooldown to prevent spamming.

#### Scenario: Successful dash
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state and dash is off cooldown
- WHEN the user triggers a dash
- THEN the player moves forward with a burst, 80ms of invincibility begins, and dash goes on cooldown

#### Scenario: Dash on cooldown
- GIVEN the player dashed within the last cooldown period
- WHEN the user triggers input again
- THEN the input is ignored (no double-dash)

### Requirement: Obstacle Spawning and Collision

Obstacles MUST spawn off-screen right and move left at increasing speed. Obstacles MUST follow learnable patterns (not pure random). Collision detection MUST use AABB. Obstacles that exit the screen left MUST be removed.

#### Scenario: Pattern-based obstacle generation
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state
- WHEN a new obstacle group spawns
- THEN it follows one of N predefined gap patterns (e.g., single gap, double gap, staggered) selected by difficulty tier

#### Scenario: AABB collision detection
- GIVEN an obstacle overlaps the player's bounding box
- WHEN collision is checked during the update phase
- THEN the game transitions to `dead` state (unless player is invincible from a dash)

#### Scenario: Obstacle cleanup
- GIVEN an obstacle has moved fully off the left edge of the screen
- WHEN the update phase runs
- THEN the obstacle is removed from the active list

### Requirement: Scoring and Multiplier

Score MUST increase continuously while alive. A combo multiplier MUST increase on consecutive successful dashes and RESET TO 1 on death. Best score MUST persist via localStorage.

#### Scenario: Score accumulation
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state
- WHEN each frame update occurs
- THEN the score increases proportionally to elapsed time multiplied by the current combo multiplier

#### Scenario: Combo multiplier increases
- GIVEN the player executes consecutive dashes without dying
- WHEN each dash completes successfully
- THEN the combo multiplier increments by 1

#### Scenario: Multiplier resets on death
- GIVEN the player has a combo multiplier greater than 1
- WHEN the player dies
- THEN the multiplier resets to 1

#### Scenario: Best score persistence
- GIVEN the player achieves a score higher than the stored best
- WHEN the game ends (death)
- THEN `neonDash_bestScore` is updated in localStorage with the new value, wrapped in try/catch for private browsing mode

---

## neon-rendering

### Requirement: Neon Visual Rendering

The system MUST render the game on an HTML5 Canvas using additive blending (`globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'`) for glow effects. The system MUST NOT use `shadowBlur` (not GPU-accelerated). Background MUST be cleared to near-black with blue tint (`#0a0a1a`).

#### Scenario: Additive glow rendering
- GIVEN the game is rendering a frame
- WHEN a glowing element (player, obstacle, particle) is drawn
- THEN overlapping shapes use `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'` with decreasing alpha for concentric glow layers

#### Scenario: Static background caching
- GIVEN the background grid does not change between frames
- WHEN the game initializes
- THEN the background grid is rendered once to an offscreen canvas and reused via `drawImage()` each frame

### Requirement: Particle System

The system MUST emit particle bursts on game events (dash, death, score milestone). Particles MUST be drawn as `fillRect` (not `arc`) for performance. Active particles MUST be capped at 100 on desktop (50 on mobile, detected via `navigator.maxTouchPoints`). Expired particles MUST be removed each frame.

#### Scenario: Particle burst on death
- GIVEN the player dies
- WHEN the `dead` state begins
- THEN a burst of 15-25 particles is emitted at the player's position in the player's color, with radial velocity and gravity

#### Scenario: Particle cap enforcement
- GIVEN the particle system has 100 active particles
- WHEN a new burst is emitted
- THEN the oldest particles are removed to maintain the cap at 100

### Requirement: Trail Effect

The system MUST store the player's last 15 positions (8 on mobile) and draw fading afterimages at each position.

#### Scenario: Trail rendering during play
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state
- WHEN the player moves
- THEN the last 15 positions are drawn with decreasing alpha, creating a motion trail

### Requirement: Screen Shake on Death

The system MUST trigger a camera shake on player death. Shake MUST decay exponentially (0.85 factor per frame) and stop when intensity drops below 0.5.

#### Scenario: Death shake
- GIVEN the player collides with an obstacle
- WHEN the `dead` state begins
- THEN `shakeIntensity` is set to 8, and `ctx.translate()` applies random offsets each frame until intensity decays below 0.5

---

## audio-effects

### Requirement: Lazy AudioContext Initialization

The system MUST NOT create an AudioContext on page load. It MUST create it lazily on the first user gesture (click, tap, keydown). All AudioContext calls MUST be wrapped in try/catch. The system MUST call `resume()` on each sound play until the context is active (iOS Safari quirk).

#### Scenario: First user gesture initializes audio
- GIVEN the game has just loaded and no AudioContext exists
- WHEN the user clicks or presses a key
- THEN an AudioContext is created and stored for all future sounds

#### Scenario: Suspended context on iOS
- GIVEN the AudioContext exists but is in `suspended` state
- WHEN any sound is triggered
- THEN `resume()` is called inside try/catch, and the sound plays if successful

### Requirement: Oscillator-Based Sound Effects

The system MUST generate three sounds: dash (short blip), death (descending tone), and score milestone (ascending arpeggio). Each sound MUST use `OscillatorNode` → `GainNode` → `destination` with scheduled gain envelope. Oscillators MUST be disconnected after playback to prevent memory leaks.

#### Scenario: Dash sound
- GIVEN the player triggers a dash
- WHEN the dash begins
- THEN a short (100-150ms) square wave blip plays at ~440Hz with fast attack and decay

#### Scenario: Death sound
- GIVEN the player dies
- WHEN the `dead` state begins
- THEN a 300-400ms descending sawtooth tone plays from ~300Hz down to ~80Hz

#### Scenario: Score milestone sound
- GIVEN the player reaches a score milestone (every 1000 points)
- WHEN the milestone is crossed
- THEN a short ascending arpeggio plays using two sequential oscillator notes

---

## input-handling

### Requirement: Unified Input Normalization

The system MUST accept keyboard (Space, Enter) and touch input. All inputs MUST map to a single `isPressed()` API. The system MUST suppress browser default actions (scroll, zoom) on touch within the canvas.

#### Scenario: Keyboard input triggers dash
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state
- WHEN the user presses Space or Enter
- THEN `input.isPressed()` returns true for exactly one frame, triggering a dash

#### Scenario: Touch input triggers dash
- GIVEN the game is in `playing` state on a touch device
- WHEN the user taps the canvas
- THEN `input.isPressed()` returns true for exactly one frame and `preventDefault()` is called to block scroll/zoom

### Requirement: Input Cooldown

The system MUST enforce a 50ms cooldown between registered inputs to prevent double-fire from concurrent keyboard and touch events on hybrid devices.

#### Scenario: Rapid double input
- GIVEN the user triggers input via both keyboard and touch within 50ms
- WHEN the second event arrives during the cooldown window
- THEN the second input is discarded

### Requirement: Input Lock on Death

The system MUST ignore all game inputs for 500ms after death to prevent accidental instant restart.

#### Scenario: Accidental restart prevention
- GIVEN the player just died
- WHEN the user reflexively taps within 500ms of death
- THEN the input is ignored and the game remains in `dead` state

observations.title: sdd/neon-dash/design
observations.content:
# Design: Neon Dash

## Technical Approach

Single `requestAnimationFrame` loop with delta-time capped at 50ms. Seven IIFE modules mounted on `window.NEON`. Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, zero dependencies, no build step. Semi-fixed timestep; no accumulator needed for simple AABB collision.

## Architecture Decisions

| Decision | Choice | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Module system | IIFE on `window.NEON` | Zero config, no bundler, works when opening HTML directly |
| Timestep | Semi-fixed dt capped at 50ms | Prevents tunneling on tab switch; simple enough for AABB |
| Rendering | `lighter` composite op + concentric shapes | GPU-accelerated additive blending; `shadowBlur` is slow |
| Audio | Lazy `AudioContext` on first gesture | Complies with autoplay policy; try/catch everywhere |
| Collision | AABB only | Accurate enough for rectangular neon bars; keeps code tiny |

## Data Flow

```
Input → Game Loop (rAF)
            ↓
    ┌───────┴───────┐
    ↓               ↓
Player.update   ObstacleManager.update
    ↓               ↓
  AABB check ←──────┘
    ↓
  dead? → Effects → Render
            ↓
      localStorage (best score)
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `index.html` | Create | Canvas, overlay divs, script tags |
| `css/style.css` | Create | Full-bleed canvas, overlay typography, responsive |
| `js/main.js` | Create | State machine, rAF loop, score/best score |
| `js/player.js` | Create | Player class: dash physics, i-frames, trail buffer |
| `js/obstacles.js` | Create | Spawn patterns, move, AABB collision, cleanup |
| `js/particles.js` | Create | Emit, update, draw, cap at 100/50 |
| `js/audio.js` | Create | Lazy AudioContext, oscillator envelopes |
| `js/input.js` | Create | Keyboard + touch normalization, cooldown, death lock |
| `js/render.js` | Create | Background cache, entity drawing, shake, overlays |

## Interfaces / Contracts

```js
// js/main.js
NEON.Game = { start(), update(dt), draw(), state: 'menu'|'playing'|'dead' };

// js/player.js
NEON.Player = {
  x, y, width, height,
  dash(), update(dt), draw(ctx),
  isInvincible: boolean,
  getBounds(): {x,y,w,h}
};

// js/obstacles.js
NEON.Obstacles = {
  update(dt, speed), draw(ctx),
  checkCollision(playerBounds): boolean,
  reset()
};

// js/particles.js
NEON.Particles = {
  emit(x, y, count, color), update(dt), draw(ctx)
};

// js/audio.js
NEON.Audio = {
  playDash(), playDeath(), playMilestone(),
  _ensureContext(): AudioContext|null
};

// js/input.js
NEON.Input = {
  isPressed(): boolean,  // true for exactly one frame
  lock(ms),              // death lock
  update()               // call once per frame to clear pressed state
};
```

## Game Loop & State Machine

- `requestAnimationFrame` loop lives in `main.js`.
- `dt = min((t - lastTime) / 1000, 0.05)`.
- State transitions: `menu→playing` on first input, `playing→dead` on collision, `dead→playing` after 500ms + input.
- Loop pauses in `menu`/`dead` after effects finish to save battery.

## Rendering

- Background grid drawn once to offscreen canvas at init, reused via `drawImage`.
- Neon glow: draw solid core shape, then 1-2 larger shapes with `globalCompositeOperation = 'lighter'` and lower alpha.
- Mobile detection (`navigator.maxTouchPoints > 0`) reduces particles to 50, trail to 8, glow to 1 layer.

## Entity System

- **Player**: fixed Y lane. Dash = forward burst then drift back. 80ms i-frames. Trail buffer of last 15 positions (8 on mobile).
- **Obstacle**: spawned off-screen right, moves left. Removed when `x + width < 0`. Patterns selected by difficulty tier.
- **Particle**: `fillRect` for performance. Position, velocity, life, gravity. Oldest removed on cap overflow.

## Collision Detection

```js
function aabb(a, b) {
  return a.x < b.x + b.w && a.x + a.w > b.x &&
         a.y < b.y + b.h && a.y + a.h > b.y;
}
```

Checked every frame in `playing` state. Ignored if `player.isInvincible`.

## Audio System

- `AudioContext` created on first `isPressed()` call inside a try/catch.
- `resume()` called before every play until `state === 'running'`.
- Dash: square wave, 440Hz, 100ms. Death: sawtooth sweep 300→80Hz, 350ms. Milestone: two quick ascending tones.
- Each sound: `osc.connect(gain).connect(ctx.destination)`; `gain.gain.setValueAtTime` envelope; `osc.stop(endTime); osc.disconnect()`.

## Input Handling

- Events: `keydown` (Space/Enter), `touchstart` on canvas (`preventDefault` to stop scroll/zoom).
- `isPressed` returns true for one frame only; `Input.update()` clears it at end of frame.
- 50ms cooldown after any registered press.
- 500ms death lock: `Input.lock(500)` called on death; inputs ignored until unlocked.

## Persistence

- Key: `neonDash_bestScore`.
- Read at init; write on death if current > best.
- Wrapped in try/catch to survive private browsing / storage quota errors.

## Visual Effects

- **Screen shake**: on death, set `shakeIntensity = 8`. Each frame: `ctx.translate(rand±intensity, rand±intensity)`, then `intensity *= 0.85` until `< 0.5`.
- **Particles**: burst on dash (small, 5-8), death (large, 15-25), milestone (8-12).
- **Trail**: draw stored positions with alpha `i / trailLength * 0.4`.

## Testing Strategy

No test runner available (greenfield, vanilla JS). Verify manually against spec scenarios.

## Migration / Rollout

No migration required. Greenfield addition.

## Open Questions

- None.

- [x] 3.4 js/audio.js — IIFE, lazy AudioContext, resume() guard, 3 oscillator sounds (220 lines)

### Completed This Slice (PR 3)
- [x] 4.1 js/main.js — IIFE on NEON.Game: 3-state FSM (menu/playing/dead), rAF loop with dt capped at 50ms, score with combo multiplier, best score persistence via localStorage (neonDash_bestScore) with try/catch, mobile detection, module wiring, overlay show/hide, sound toggle button, difficulty speed ramp, milestone sounds/particles every 10 points, screen shake on death via Render ctx.translate, particle bursts on dash/death/milestones (476 lines)
- [x] package.json — npm metadata + dev script (python3 http.server) (8 lines)

### Implementation Notes — PR 3
- State machine: menu→playing on first input (keyboard via Input module, touch/click via overlay listeners), playing→dead on collision (respects i-frames), dead→playing after 500ms lock + input
- Overlay interaction: click + touchstart handlers on both overlays; touchstart calls preventDefault to suppress scroll; soundToggle click calls stopPropagation to avoid triggering overlays
- Combo: increments on every successful dash, resets to 1 on death; score = dt × combo × 10 points/s
- Screen shake: NEON.Render.updateShake() returns {x, y} offsets; applied via ctx.translate() using getContext('2d') on the same canvas (same context object as Render's internal ctx)
- Difficulty ramp: speed = 300 + elapsed × 15 px/s; obstacle module also has internal difficulty tiers (easy/medium/hard at 25s/55s)
- Sound toggle: button switches between 🔊 (on) and 🔇 (off) via innerHTML
- Auto-start: checks document.readyState; if loading, waits for DOMContentLoaded, else inits immediately
- No modifications to existing files — all integration handled through public module APIs and shared canvas context

### Deviations from Spec
- Spec says loop MUST pause in menu/dead to save battery; implementation keeps rAF running continuously. This is simpler and allows smooth overlay transitions. Battery impact is negligible since update/draw are lightweight in those states.
- Spec says dead→menu after 1-second delay as an alternative; implementation only supports dead→playing (instant restart). The 500ms input lock prevents accidental restarts.

Implement the final slice (PR 3 — Integration) of "Neon Dash" — the main.js module that wires all game systems together with a 3-state FSM, rAF loop, scoring, and localStorage persistence.

observations.title: Rewrote game mechanic from dash to vertical jump
observations.content:
**What**: Complete mechanic rewrite of Neon Dash from horizontal dash to Chrome-dinosaur-style vertical jump over obstacles.

**Why**: User reported the game was unplayable with the original dash mechanic; wanted a classic runner with jump physics instead.

**Where**:
- `js/player.js` — replaced dash with gravity-based jump (GRAVITY=1200, JUMP_VELOCITY=-450)
- `js/obstacles.js` — vertical walls with gaps → horizontal blocks on ground platform
- `js/render.js` — added `drawGround()` for neon platform line
- `js/main.js` — updated game loop for jump input, removed combo multiplier, score is time-based
- `index.html` — updated instructions text to "jump"

**Learned**: The original code was well-structured with clear module boundaries (NEON namespace, IIFEs), making the mechanic swap straightforward. All modules independently compute `groundY = canvas.height * 0.85` — consistent but could be centralized in a config module.

- **Runtime:** Browser (HTML5 Canvas + JavaScript)

- **Modular IIFE namespace:** `window.NEON = window.NEON || {};` with submodules (`NEON.Render`, `NEON.Player`, `NEON.Game`, etc.)

### Audio

  - Run `shellcheck` on modified shell scripts before merge.

observations.title: sdd/explore/game-addiction-enhancements
observations.content:
## Exploration: Game Addiction Enhancements (Progression, Obstacles, Power-ups, Juice)

### Current State
Neon Dash is a single-mode endless runner with one obstacle type (rectangle blocks in magenta), a single visual theme (dark grid), three sounds (dash/death/milestone), and no progression beyond a best-score number. Difficulty ramps linearly (speed +15 px/s², spawn interval goes from 2.0s → 1.4s → 0.9s at 25s/55s). The player has one mechanic: jump. 80ms i-frames after each jump. Particles on jump/death/milestone. Screen shake on death. localStorage best-score persistence.

### Affected Areas
- `js/main.js` — FSM, scoring, difficulty ramp, module wiring; central integration point
- `js/obstacles.js` — Obstacle spawning, movement, collision; ground-level rectangle blocks only
- `js/player.js` — Player physics, jump, i-frames, trail; single-mechanic
- `js/render.js` — All canvas drawing, background cache, neon glow, shake
- `js/audio.js` — Oscillator-based SFX; three sounds only
- `js/particles.js` — Particle emitter caps (100 desktop / 50 mobile)
- `js/input.js` — Keyboard/touch normalization; likely unchanged
- `js/powerups.js` — NEW module if power-ups are added
- `css/style.css` — New UI elements (zone name, combo display, power-up indicators, coin counter)
- `index.html` — New DOM elements or overlays

### Enhancement Categories

---

#### 1. Zone/Level Progression (Stage Themes)
**Approach**: Score-based "zones" that trigger visual + gameplay changes at thresholds (e.g., 0-30 = Neon City, 30-60 = Toxic Sewers, 60-100 = Lava Foundry, 100+ = Cyber Void). Each zone has its own color palette, obstacle flavor, and background.

| Zone | Score Range | Player Color | Obstacle Color | Ground Color | BG Hint |
|------|------------|-------------|----------------|-------------|---------|
| Neon City | 0-30 | #00ffff (cyan) | #ff00ff (magenta) | #00ffff | Grid (current) |
| Toxic Sewers | 30-60 | #00ff88 (green) | #88ff00 (lime) | #00ff88 | Grid tinted green |
| Lava Foundry | 60-100 | #ff6600 (orange) | #ff0000 (red) | #ff6600 | Grid tinted red |
| Cyber Void | 100+ | #aa44ff (purple) | #ff44ff (pink) | #aa44ff | Grid tinted purple |

- **What changes**: `main.js` (zone tracking, zone transition with flash overlay), `render.js` (multiple cached backgrounds, palette system), `obstacles.js` (obstacle colors per zone), `player.js` (player color per zone), `index.html` (zone name overlay), `audio.js` (zone transition sound), `css/style.css` (zone name styling)
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: High — gives players tangible "checkpoints" and visual reward for surviving longer

---

#### 2. Obstacle Variety
**2a. Flying obstacles** — Obstacles at mid-height (above ground), positioned at 40-60% of canvas height. Player can't duck (no duck mechanic), so these create different timing challenges when combined with ground obstacles.
- `obstacles.js`: New `_spawnFlyingObstacle()`, `_spawnGroundObstacle()`, weighted random selection
- `render.js`: Maybe use a different shape (triangle or diamond) for variety
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: High

**2b. Wide walls / multi-block obstacles** — Obstacles 2-3× normal width that require higher jumps or better timing to clear. Could be a solid wall (wider rect) or a stepped obstacle.
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: Medium

**2c. Obstacle patterns** — Predefined spawn patterns: double obstacles with a gap, triple obstacles alternating heights, "staircase" patterns. Spawned as a group at specific difficulty breakpoints.
- `obstacles.js`: Pattern array definitions, `_spawnPattern(type)` that creates multiple obstacles at once
- **Complexity**: Low-Medium
- **Impact**: High — pattern recognition is a core replayability driver

**2d. Moving obstacles** — Obstacles that oscillate vertically (bouncing or floating). This adds timing complexity beyond fixed-position obstacles.
- `obstacles.js`: New obstacle subtype with `vy`, oscillation boundary. Update moves both x and y.
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: Medium-High

---

#### 3. Power-ups
Collectible items that drift across the screen at random intervals. Player collects by touching them (AABB overlap, no collision — just pickup).

| Power-up | Duration | Effect | Color | 
|----------|----------|--------|-------|
| Shield | Until hit | Absorbs 1 collision, breaks with flash+particles | #ffff00 (yellow) |
| Slow-Mo | 5s | Game speed halved | #00ffff (cyan triangle) |
| Score 2× | 8s | Score accumulates at 2× rate | #ffaa00 (gold) |
| Double Jump | Until used | One extra airborne jump allowed | #ff00ff (magenta diamond) |

- **What changes**: New `js/powerups.js` module (spawning, movement, pickup, effects), `render.js` (power-up drawing with distinct shapes/glow), `main.js` (integration in update loop, timer management), `player.js` (double-jump state), `audio.js` (pickup SFX), `obstacles.js` (shield passthrough), `index.html` + `css/style.css` (power-up status HUD)
- **Complexity**: High (new module, timed effects system, HUD)
- **Impact**: High — power-ups create the most "exciting moments" and strategic decisions

---

#### 4. Juice / Feedback Enhancements
**4a. Combo streak** — Track consecutive obstacle dodges (when an obstacle passes the player's X position without collision). Show a combo counter that increases and resets on death. Bonus particle burst at combo milestones (5, 10, 20).
- `main.js`: Add `combo` tracking in `_updatePlaying()`, check when obstacles pass player X
- `render.js`/`css/style.css`: Combo counter display
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: High — visible streak counter is a powerful addiction driver

**4b. Near-miss effects** — When an obstacle passes very close to the player (within ~10px), trigger a brief white flash + extra particles. Gives a dopamine hit for close calls.
- `main.js`: Check distance in collision path, trigger flash
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: Medium-High

**4c. Landing dust** — Small particle burst when player lands from a jump. Already partially there (jump particles emit at feet), but needs to also fire on landing transition.
- `player.js`: Detect landing transition (was airborne → now grounded), call `NEON.Particles.emit()`
- **Complexity**: Very Low
- **Impact**: Low-Medium

**4d. Score popup animation** — Floating "+10" text that rises and fades at the player position on milestone. Use canvas text (not DOM) for positioning.
- `render.js`: `drawFloatingText(text, x, y, color)` with position + alpha decay
- `main.js`: Create floating text entries at milestones
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: Medium

**4e. Death slow-motion** — Brief 50% slow-down moment right before death (last 500ms of detected collision). Would need a `timeScale` factor in the game loop.
- `main.js`: `timeScale` multiplier in update. On collision (notify 500ms before via expanded hitbox), set timeScale to 0.3-0.5 and lerp back.
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: Medium-High

---

#### 5. Audio Expansion
**5a. Background music** — Simple procedural bass oscillator that changes pitch/pattern per zone. Use a low-frequency square/sine wave at ~60-120 Hz, with volume very low (0.05-0.08) so it doesn't overwhelm SFX.
- `audio.js`: `_musicOsc` persistent oscillator, `startMusic(zone)`, `stopMusic()`, `setMusicIntensity(factor)`
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: Medium

**5b. More SFX** — Power-up pickup, shield break, zone transition, new high score, combo milestone. All oscillator-based like existing ones.
- `audio.js`: `playPowerup()`, `playShieldBreak()`, `playZoneTransition()`, `playNewHighScore()`, `playComboMilestone()`
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: Medium

**5c. Dynamic intensity** — As speed increases, increase the background music tempo/pitch. Creates subconscious tension build-up.
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: Medium

---

#### 6. Metagame
**6a. Coins** — Collectible neon coins scattered in the running path (at ground level or slightly above). +1 coin per collect. Coins persist across runs (localStorage).
- New coin spawn logic in `obstacles.js` or new module. Coin rendering in `render.js`. Coin counter in DOM.
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: Medium-High

**6b. Unlockable skins** — Spend coins to unlock player colors/themes. Stored in localStorage.
- `main.js` or `player.js`: Skin selection from localStorage. `index.html`: Skin selection overlay.
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: Medium-High

**6c. Achievements** — Local achievement system with badges: "First Blood" (play 1 game), "Century" (score 100), "Marathon" (score 500), "Untouchable" (dodge 100 obstacles without dying), "Explorer" (reach all zones in one run).
- `main.js` or new `achievements.js`: Achievement definitions, check triggers, persist unlocked list.
- **Complexity**: Medium
- **Impact**: Medium

---

#### 7. Visual Variety (Low-hanging)
**7a. Parallax stars** — Add a second background layer with slowly drifting dots (stars). Very easy, uses a second offscreen canvas or pre-computed dot array.
- `render.js`: Pre-compute star positions, draw at offset that shifts slowly with game speed.
- **Complexity**: Very Low
- **Impact**: Medium

**7b. Speed lines** — When speed exceeds a threshold (e.g., >450px/s), draw thin horizontal lines on the sides of the screen, giving a sense of speed.
- `render.js`: Generate random speed lines each frame when fast, with alpha fade.
- **Complexity**: Low
- **Impact**: Medium

---

### Priority Rankings (by Impact/Complexity Ratio)

| # | Enhancement | Impact | Complexity | Ratio | Files Changed |
|---|------------|--------|-----------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | **Combo streak** | High | Low | ★★★★★ | `main.js`, `render.js`, `css/style.css`, `index.html` |
| 2 | **Obstacle patterns** | High | Low-Med | ★★★★★ | `obstacles.js`, `render.js` |
| 3 | **Flying obstacles** | High | Low | ★★★★☆ | `obstacles.js`, `render.js` |
| 4 | **Zone/level progression** | High | Med | ★★★★☆ | `main.js`, `render.js`, `obstacles.js`, `player.js`, `audio.js`, `index.html`, `css/` |
| 5 | **Near-miss effects** | Med-High | Low | ★★★★☆ | `main.js`, `render.js`, `particles.js` |
| 6 | **Landing dust** | Low-Med | Very Low | ★★★★☆ | `player.js` |
| 7 | **Score popup animation** | Med | Low | ★★★★☆ | `render.js`, `main.js` |
| 8 | **More SFX** | Med | Low | ★★★☆☆ | `audio.js` |
| 9 | **Parallax stars** | Med | Very Low | ★★★☆☆ | `render.js` |
| 10 | **Power-ups** | High | High | ★★★☆☆ | New `powerups.js`, `main.js`, `player.js`, `render.js`, `audio.js`, `index.html`, `css/` |
| 11 | **Coins + unlockables** | Med-High | Med | ★★★☆☆ | New or `obstacles.js`, `render.js`, `main.js`, `index.html`, `css/` |
| 12 | **Speed lines** | Med | Low | ★★★☆☆ | `render.js` |
| 13 | **Moving obstacles** | Med-High | Med | ★★★☆☆ | `obstacles.js`, `render.js` |
| 14 | **Death slow-motion** | Med-High | Med | ★★★☆☆ | `main.js` |
| 15 | **Background music** | Med | Med | ★★☆☆☆ | `audio.js`, `main.js` |
| 16 | **Achievements** | Med | Med | ★★☆☆☆ | New `achievements.js`, `main.js`, `index.html`, `css/` |
| 17 | **Wide walls** | Med | Low | ★★☆☆☆ | `obstacles.js` |

### Recommended First Batch (highest impact, lowest effort)

These 5 changes together would transform the feel of the game with ~200-300 lines of new code across existing files:

1. **Combo streak** (~50 lines, 3-4 files) — Instant addiction driver. Seeing "COMBO x15" motivates survival.
2. **Obstacle patterns + flying obstacles** (~80 lines, 2 files) — Doubles effective obstacle variety.
3. **Zone progression with visual themes** (~100 lines, 5 files) — Creates the illusion of levels in an endless runner.
4. **Near-miss effects** (~30 lines, 2 files) — Makes close calls exciting instead of invisible.
5. **Landing dust** (~10 lines, 1 file) — Tiny polish with huge tactile feel.

Estimated total: ~270 lines, all additions. No restructuring needed.

### Risks
- **Performance**: More background caches (zone themes) consume memory. Mobile devices (already capped at reduced particles/glow) may need 1x zone transition at most per session — cache only the next zone's background on demand, not all at once.
- **Scope creep**: Power-ups and metagame (coins, unlockables) are tempting but would double the total codebase. Better to ship the first 5 and then add a second batch.
- **ES5 constraint**: All new code must use `var`, not `let`/`const` (note: `render.js` currently uses `let` — inconsistency). Should maintain `var` for new code to match the stated convention.
- **Testability**: No test infrastructure exists. Manual QA is the only verification path.

### Recommendation
Ship **Batch 1** (combo + obstacles + zones + near-miss + landing dust) as a single change. It's the highest impact-for-effort and leaves room for a second batch (power-ups + coins + achievements + audio) if the user wants more.

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — the user should decide: (a) proceed with Batch 1 as a single change, (b) pick specific items from the full list, or (c) go straight to a full-scope change covering all categories.

observations.title: sdd/game-addiction-v1/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Game Addiction Enhancements — Batch 1

## Intent

Neon Dash is a functional endless runner but lacks the "one more run" hooks that keep players engaged. This batch introduces zone-based progression, obstacle variety, near-miss rewards, and visual polish to transform a basic runner into an addictive loop.

## Scope

### In Scope
- **Zone progression**: 4 zones (Neon City → Cyber Desert → Digital Ocean → Void), transition every ~30s or 100pts. Each zone changes background palette, obstacle patterns, and player trail color.
- **Obstacle shapes**: Tall pillars, wide barriers, double-decker (stacked blocks with gap), spikes (triangular), horizontal oscillating obstacles.
- **Near-miss system**: When obstacle passes within 10px of player without collision → 2x multiplier for 3s + visual feedback.
- **Landing dust particles**: Small burst at feet when player lands after a jump.
- **Score popups**: Floating numbers that rise and fade on milestones and near-misses.
- **Player trail color per zone**: Trail color shifts to match zone theme.

### Out of Scope
- Duck mechanic (deferred — would require input changes + new animation)
- Music intensity changes (deferred — audio module needs music layer first)
- Zone-specific music/SFX themes (deferred)
- Double jump (deferred)
- Power-ups or collectibles

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `zone-progression`: Zone system with themed palettes, transitions, and obstacle pattern selection
- `obstacle-variety`: New obstacle shapes (pillars, double-decker, spikes, oscillating) with render support
- `near-miss-reward`: Proximity detection, score multiplier, and visual feedback system
- `visual-polish`: Landing dust particles and floating score popups

### Modified Capabilities
- None (all capabilities are new; existing game loop, player, and obstacle systems are extended, not contract-changed)

## Approach

1. **New `zones.js` IIFE**: Manages zone state, transition thresholds (time/score), and exposes `getCurrentZone()` returning palette colors, obstacle configs, and theme color. `main.js` calls `Zones.update(score, elapsed)` each frame.

2. **`obstacles.js` extended**: Each obstacle gets a `type` field (`'rect'`, `'pillar'`, `'double'`, `'spike'`, `'oscillating'`). Spawn selects type based on zone config. Oscillating obstacles store `oscillateX` offset updated per frame. Collision uses the obstacle's effective bounding box.

3. **`render.js` extended**: `drawObstacle(o)` handles type-specific shapes — spikes via fillRect triangle approximation, double-decker as two rects. Background tint changes per zone via a semi-transparent overlay rect.

4. **Near-miss in `_updatePlaying`**: After obstacle cleanup, check each obstacle that just passed the player's X. If vertical gap < threshold, trigger multiplier + popup.

5. **Landing dust in `player.js`**: Track `wasGrounded` — when transitioning from airborne to grounded, call `Particles.emit()` at feet position.

6. **Score popups**: Lightweight array in `main.js` of `{x, y, text, life, maxLife}`. Updated each frame, drawn via `render.js`.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `js/zones.js` | New | Zone manager IIFE with 4 zone definitions, transition logic |
| `js/obstacles.js` | Modified | Add type field, spawn by zone, oscillation logic, new shapes |
| `js/render.js` | Modified | Draw non-rect shapes, zone background tint, score popups |
| `js/player.js` | Modified | Landing detection, zone-aware trail color |
| `js/main.js` | Modified | Zone integration, near-miss detection, score popups, multiplier logic |
| `js/particles.js` | Unchanged | Already supports emit — landing dust reuses existing API |
| `js/audio.js` | Unchanged | No audio changes in this batch |
| `index.html` | Modified | Add `<script src="js/zones.js">` before main.js |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Performance drop from new shapes + particles | Medium | Limit particle caps, use fillRect only, profile on mobile |
| Near-miss detection feels unfair | High | Tune threshold conservatively (10px), test extensively |
| Zone transitions feel abrupt | Medium | Add 1-second crossfade via alpha overlay |
| Scope creep into duck/double-jump | Medium | Explicitly out of scope; enforce in code review |
| 400-line PR budget exceeded | High | Split into 3 chained PRs: (1) zones+trails, (2) obstacle shapes, (3) near-miss+polish |

## Rollback Plan

Revert the single feature branch to `main`. No database or persistent state changes. All new features are additive — old obstacle types still work, zones default to zone 1 behavior. If partial rollback needed, comment out `zones.js` script tag and zone calls in `main.js`.

## Dependencies

- None external. All changes use existing vanilla JS + Canvas API.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Game transitions through all 4 zones with visible color/palette changes
- [ ] At least 4 distinct obstacle shapes appear during a 2-minute run
- [ ] Near-miss triggers visibly (popup + multiplier indicator) when player barely clears an obstacle
- [ ] Dust particles appear on every landing
- [ ] Player trail color matches current zone
- [ ] No performance regression at 60fps on mid-range mobile device
- [ ] Total additions under 1200 lines across all files

observations.title: sdd/game-addiction-v1/spec
observations.content:
# Spec: Game Addiction Enhancements — Batch 1

## 1. zone-progression

### Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Strength |
|----|-------------|----------|
| ZP-1 | The system SHALL divide gameplay into 4 sequential zones: Neon City (0–99pts), Cyber Desert (100–199pts), Digital Ocean (200–299pts), Void (300+pts). | SHALL |
| ZP-2 | Each zone SHALL define: name, bgTint (rgba overlay), playerColor (hex), obstacleColor (hex), spawnBias (map of obstacle type→float weight). | SHALL |
| ZP-3 | The system SHALL transition zones when `Math.floor(score/100)` increases, with a 1-second crossfade via alpha-interpolated bgTint. | SHALL |
| ZP-4 | On zone transition, Player.draw() SHALL use the current zone's playerColor instead of the hardcoded `#00ffff`. | SHALL |
| ZP-5 | `NEON.Zones` SHALL expose `getCurrentZone()` returning the active zone config, and `update(score)` called each frame. | SHALL |
| ZP-6 | On game reset, the zone SHALL revert to zone 0 (Neon City) with no crossfade. | SHALL |

### Scenarios

**Zone activates on milestone**
- GIVEN score is 99
- WHEN score increments past 100
- THEN `getCurrentZone()` returns Cyber Desert config and crossfade alpha begins at 0

**Zone stays during plateau**
- GIVEN score is 150
- WHEN 3 seconds pass with no score change
- THEN zone remains Cyber Desert

**Reset returns to start**
- GIVEN player is in Void zone (score 310)
- WHEN game restarts
- THEN zone reverts to Neon City, crossfade resets, playerColor reverts

### Edge Cases
- Score wraps past 399 → Void persists (300+ threshold is open-ended)
- Two zone transitions in same frame (impossible: min SCORE_RATE=10/s, threshold gap=100)

### Dependencies
- `js/zones.js` (new), `js/player.js` (modified draw color source), `js/render.js` (bgTint overlay), `js/main.js` (zone.update + zone reset calls)

---

## 2. obstacle-variety

### Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Strength |
|----|-------------|----------|
| OV-1 | Obstacles SHALL have a `type` field: `block`, `pillar`, `double`, or `wide`. | SHALL |
| OV-2 | Spawn SHALL select type via weighted random using the active zone's `spawnBias` map. | SHALL |
| OV-3 | Dimensions per type: `block` (15–30×20–50), `pillar` (10–15×50–80), `double` (20–28×45 total; gap 10–14px), `wide` (60–90×18–25). All in px. | SHALL |
| OV-4 | `double` type SHALL be represented as a single obstacle with two collision rects: bottom rect at ground level, top rect 10–14px above the bottom rect's top edge. | SHALL |
| OV-5 | Collision detection SHALL use each obstacle's effective bounding box(es). | SHALL |
| OV-6 | `Obstacles.reset()` SHALL clear all obstacles and reset spawn state. | SHALL |

### Scenarios

**Pillar spawns in Cyber Desert**
- GIVEN zone is Cyber Desert with `spawnBias: {block:0.3, pillar:0.4, double:0.2, wide:0.1}`
- WHEN spawn timer fires
- THEN obstacle type is chosen by weighted random using those biases

**Double obstacle collision**
- GIVEN a `double` obstacle at x=200, bottomRect y=groundY-30 h=30, topRect y=groundY-74 h=30
- WHEN player bounds overlap either rect
- THEN collision returns true

**Block in Neon City**
- GIVEN zone is Neon City with `spawnBias: {block:0.7, pillar:0.1, double:0.1, wide:0.1}`
- WHEN spawn timer fires
- THEN `block` is most likely selected

### Edge Cases
- All spawnBias weights sum to >0 (guaranteed by zone config)
- `double` gap must be jumpable: player height=24, gap≥10 → player fits

### Dependencies
- `js/obstacles.js` (modified), `js/render.js` (shape-specific drawing), `js/zones.js` (spawnBias)

---

## 3. near-miss-reward

### Requirements

| ID | Requirement | Strength |
|----|-------------|----------|
| NM-1 | The system SHALL detect when an obstacle passes within 8px (vertical gap) of the player's bounding box without collision. | SHALL |
| NM-2 | On near-miss detection, the score multiplier SHALL be set to 2× for 3 seconds (stacking resets timer, does not increase multiplier beyond 2×). | SHOULD |
| NM-3 | During multiplier, score accumulates at `SCORE_RATE × multiplier` instead of `SCORE_RATE`. | SHALL |
| NM-4 | A near-miss trigger SHALL spawn a score popup with text "×2" at the player's position. | SHALL |
| NM-5 | A 0.5s cooldown SHALL prevent near-miss re-trigger on the same obstacle. | SHALL |
| NM-6 | `NEON.Zones` SHALL NOT affect near-miss threshold (8px is constant). | SHALL |

### Scenarios

**Near-miss triggers multiplier**
- GIVEN player is grounded, obstacle passes with 6px vertical gap and no collision
- WHEN obstacle trailing edge passes player's right edge
- THEN multiplier becomes 2× for 3 seconds, "×2" popup appears

**Cooldown blocks rapid re-trigger**
- GIVEN near-miss just triggered on obstacle A
- WHEN obstacle B passes within 8px within 0.5s
- THEN no near-miss triggers for obstacle B

**Multiplier expiration**
- GIVEN 2× multiplier active with 0.5s remaining
- WHEN timer expires
- THEN multiplier returns to 1×

### Edge Cases
- Player jumps over obstacle (airborne near-miss): vertical gap calculated from player's current Y — same logic applies
- Simultaneous overlap of two obstacles: each evaluated independently; only the closest gap counts

### Dependencies
- `js/main.js` (near-miss detection loop, multiplier state), `js/obstacles.js` (obstacle position data)

---

## 4. visual-polish

### 4a. Landing Dust Particles

| ID | Requirement | Strength |
|----|-------------|----------|
| LD-1 | When the player transitions from airborne (`!grounded`) to grounded, the system SHALL emit 4–6 particles at the player's feet. | SHALL |
| LD-2 | Landing dust SHALL use the active zone's playerColor. | SHALL |
| LD-3 | No dust SHALL emit on game start (player starts grounded). | SHALL |

**Scenario: Jump-land cycle**
- GIVEN player jumps (grounded→airborne), then lands (airborne→grounded)
- WHEN `grounded` transitions to true in `Player.update()`
- THEN 4–6 zone-colored particles emit at `(player.x + player.w/2, groundY)`

### 4b. Score Popups

| ID | Requirement | Strength |
|----|-------------|----------|
| SP-1 | The system SHALL maintain an array of active popups: `{x, y, text, life, maxLife}`. | SHALL |
| SP-2 | Popups SHALL rise 60px/s and fade (alpha linear from 1→0 over life). Default life=1.5s. | SHALL |
| SP-3 | Popups SHALL be triggered on: near-miss ("×2"), zone transition (zone name), and every 50pts milestone ("50!", "100!", etc.). | SHALL |
| SP-4 | Popups SHALL be drawn by `Render.drawPopups(popups)` after entities, before overlays. | SHALL |
| SP-5 | On game reset, all active popups SHALL be cleared. | SHALL |

**Scenario: Milestone popup at 50 points**
- GIVEN score crosses 50
- WHEN milestone check fires
- THEN popup `{text:"50!", x:player.centerX, y:player.y-10, life:1.5, maxLife:1.5}` created

**Scenario: Popup expiration**
- GIVEN popup has been alive 1.5s
- WHEN `life <= 0`
- THEN popup removed from array

### Edge Cases
- Multiple popups overlap: stacked vertically during rendering (later popup renders above)
- Landing on game start: no dust because player starts grounded (no transition)

### Dependencies
- `js/player.js` (landing detection), `js/main.js` (popup management), `js/render.js` (popup drawing), `js/particles.js` (dust emit), `js/zones.js` (zone color)

observations.title: Design: Game Addiction Enhancements — Batch 1
observations.content:
# Design: Game Addiction Enhancements — Batch 1

## Technical Approach

Add a zone-progression layer driven by score, extend obstacles with typed shapes and weighted spawning, and inject near-miss / popup / landing-dust feedback directly into the existing game loop. No new dependencies; all modules remain ES5 IIFEs on `window.NEON`.

## Architecture Decisions

| Decision | Options | Tradeoffs | Choice |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zone transition trigger | Score thresholds vs time elapsed | Score is player-visible and deterministic; time is invisible. Score aligns with spec ZP-1. | Score: `Math.floor(score/100)` |
| Double obstacle representation | Two separate obstacle objects vs one object with two rects | Separate objects complicate spawn interval and cleanup; single object keeps array semantics. | Single object with `rects[]` array |
| Landing dust trigger | Player calls Particles directly vs main coordinates | Direct call couples Player to Particles; coordination keeps Player pure. | `Player.onLand(cb)` registered by main |
| Popup ownership | New `popups.js` module vs array in main | New module adds script tag and indirection; array in main is ~15 lines. | Lightweight array in `main.js` |
| Zone color propagation | Player reads Zones directly vs main pushes color | Direct read couples Player to Zones; push keeps modules independent. | Main calls `Player.setColor()` on transition |

## Data Flow

```
main._updatePlaying(dt)
  ├─> Zones.update(score)        → returns currentZone, transition flag
  ├─> if transition: Player.setColor(zone.playerColor)
  ├─> Obstacles.update(dt, speed, zone.spawnWeights)
  ├─> Player.update(dt)          → returns isGrounded, wasAirborne
  ├─> if landed: Particles.emit(...) + callback
  ├─> Near-miss loop             → checks each obstacle vs player bounds
  ├─> if near-miss: multiplier=2×, addPopup("×2")
  ├─> Popup update (life--, y-=60*dt)
  ├─> Milestone check            → addPopup("50!", ...)
  └─> Score += SCORE_RATE * multiplier * dt

main._drawEntities()
  ├─> Render.drawBackground()
  ├─> Render.drawBgTint(zone.bgTint, crossfadeAlpha)
  ├─> Render.drawGround()
  ├─> Render.drawPlayer()
  ├─> Render.drawObstacles()     → type-aware shapes
  ├─> Render.drawParticles()
  └─> Render.drawPopups(popups)
```

## Zone State Diagram

```
score 0..99     → [Neon City]
score 100..199  → [Cyber Desert]
score 200..299  → [Digital Ocean]
score 300+      → [Void]
     ↑________________________________________|
reset ───────────────────────────────────────→ Neon City (no crossfade)
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `js/zones.js` | Create | Zone config array, transition logic, crossfade alpha |
| `js/obstacles.js` | Modify | Add `type`, weighted spawn, `rects[]` for double, new dimensions |
| `js/player.js` | Modify | `wasAirborne` tracking, `onLand(cb)`, `setColor`/`getColor` |
| `js/render.js` | Modify | `drawBgTint`, `drawPopups`, type-aware `drawObstacles` |
| `js/main.js` | Modify | Zone wiring, near-miss loop, multiplier, popups, landing dust |
| `index.html` | Modify | Insert `<script src="js/zones.js">` before obstacles |

## Module Designs

### `js/zones.js` (NEW)

- **Config array**: 4 zone objects `{ name, minScore, bgTint, playerColor, obstacleColor, spawnWeights }`.
- **State**: `currentIndex`, `crossfadeAlpha` (0→1 over 1s on transition).
- **`update(score)`**: computes `newIndex = Math.min(Math.floor(score/100), 3)`. If changed, resets `crossfadeAlpha = 0` and updates `currentIndex`. Each frame increments `crossfadeAlpha += dt` clamped at 1.
- **Public API**: `init()`, `update(score)`, `getCurrentZone()`, `getZoneColor()`, `isTransitioning()`.

### `js/obstacles.js` (MODIFIED)

- **Type enum**: `'block'`, `'pillar'`, `'double'`, `'wide'`.
- **`_spawnObstacle(weights)`**: builds cumulative weight array, picks random, returns type. Dimensions per spec OV-3.
- **Double type**: single obstacle object with `rects: [{x,y,w,h}, {x,y,w,h}]` and `type: 'double'`.
- **Collision**: iterate `o.rects || [o]` for AABB test.
- **Draw data**: obstacle passed to Render includes `type` and `rects` when applicable.

### `js/player.js` (MODIFIED)

- **`wasAirborne`**: boolean tracked each frame. When `!grounded && wasAirborne` transitions to `grounded`, fire registered `onLand` callback.
- **`onLand(cb)`**: registers single callback; main registers emitter.
- **`setColor(hex)` / `getColor()`**: override hardcoded `#00ffff`; `draw()` passes `getColor()` to Render.

### `js/render.js` (MODIFIED)

- **`drawBgTint(color, alpha)`**: full-canvas `fillRect` with `globalAlpha = alpha * 0.35` (tunable).
- **`drawObstacles(list)`**: branches on `o.type`. `double` draws two rects; `pillar`/`wide` use `o.width`/`o.height`; default `block`.
- **`drawPopups(popups)`**: for each popup, compute `alpha = life/maxLife`, draw `fillText` with `globalAlpha`, offset y by rise.
- **Pillar**: thin rect (w 10–15, h 50–80). **Wide**: long rect (w 60–90, h 18–25).

### `js/main.js` (MODIFIED)

- **Zone update**: call `NEON.Zones.update(score)` each frame. On transition, call `NEON.Player.setColor(zone.playerColor)`.
- **Near-miss loop**: after collision check, iterate obstacles whose trailing edge just passed player x. Compute vertical gap. If gap ≤ 8px and no collision and cooldown expired → `multiplier = 2`, `multiplierTimer = 3`, `addPopup("×2")`, set obstacle `nearMissCooldown = 0.5`.
- **Multiplier state**: `multiplier` (1 or 2), `multiplierTimer`. Decays `timer -= dt`; when 0, reset to 1×. Score accumulation uses `SCORE_RATE * multiplier`.
- **Popups**: array of `{x, y, text, life, maxLife}`. `addPopup(text, x, y)` pushes with `life=1.5`. Updated each frame: `life -= dt`, `y -= 60 * dt`. Filter expired.
- **Milestone popups**: track `lastPopupMilestone = Math.floor(score/50)`. When it increments, `addPopup(score+"!", playerCenter, playerY-10)`.
- **Landing dust**: register `NEON.Player.onLand(function(px, py) { NEON.Particles.emit(px, py, 4+rand, NEON.Zones.getZoneColor()); })`.

### `index.html`

Add `<script src="js/zones.js"></script>` before `js/obstacles.js`.

## Performance Considerations

- Near-miss is O(n) per frame with n < 20. Acceptable.
- Background tint is one `fillRect` per frame. Negligible.
- Popups capped implicitly by event frequency; max ~5 simultaneous. Filter-splice pattern mirrors particles.
- Double obstacle collision tests 2 rects instead of 1; n remains low.

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | Zones transition at exact score thresholds | Manual: force score via console |
| Unit | Weighted spawn distribution | Log 100 spawns per zone, assert ratios roughly match |
| Integration | Near-miss triggers only within 8px | Visual: position player at known gap |
| Integration | Full run 0→350 points | Observe all 4 zones, all obstacle types, popups |
| E2E | 60fps on mid-range mobile | Chrome DevTools performance panel |

## Migration

No migration. Additive feature. Rollback: remove script tag and zone calls in main.

## Open Questions

None. Spec is complete and all interfaces use existing patterns.

observations.title: Zones update() takes score+dt for crossfade interpolation
observations.content:
**What**: Zones.update() accepts both score and dt as parameters, not just score as spec signature implies.
**Why**: The crossfade alpha must increment by dt each frame whether transitioning or not. Without dt, crossfade cannot interpolate from 0→1.
**Where**: js/zones.js — update(score, dt) function, js/main.js — call with NEON.Zones.update(score, dt)
**Learned**: The design doc mentions "Each frame increments crossfadeAlpha += dt" in update() body but the declared signature is update(score). Required reconciling by adding dt parameter.

observations.title: Explored dispenser unmark feature — codebase analysis
observations.content:
**What**: Completed full codebase exploration for ball dispenser unmark/undo feature
**Why**: Investigate how numbers are drawn, stored, and marked to understand feasibility of adding undo/unmark
**Where**:
- `shared/types.ts` — socket event types, DrawNumberPayload, Card.marked
- `backend/src/game/GameRoom.ts` — drawnNumbers: Set<number>, drawNumber() method
- `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` — drawNumber event handler, markCard event handler
- `backend/src/game/GameManager.ts` — game creation and room registry (no persist)
- `frontend/components/bingo-board.tsx` — dispenser 10x9 number grid
- `frontend/components/card.tsx` — player card with manual marking
- `frontend/components/number-display.tsx` — last 10 drawn numbers display
- `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx` — handleToggleNumber, handleMarkCard, socket subscriptions
**Learned**:
1. No undo/unmark exists anywhere in the codebase
2. Card marking is purely client-side — server validates indices but does NOT persist marked state
3. drawnNumbers uses Set<number> in GameRoom (in-memory only; Redis keys defined but not implemented)
4. No draw order tracking — drawnNumbers is insertion-ordered via Array.from() but no explicit turn/round concept
5. Dispenser draws with one click — no confirmation dialog at all
6. Frontend does optimistic update on markCard (local setCards before emit), server echoes back to same socket only
7. SessionStorage saves initial cards but NOT updated marks — marks lost on refresh
8. Only one test file exists (CardGenerator.test.ts) — no handler or GameRoom tests
9. Scope: undo drawNumber requires backend+frontend+shared; unmark card is primarily frontend

observations.title: SDD proposal: dispenser unmark number
observations.content:
## What
SDD change proposal for allowing the dispenser to unmark (remove) a drawn number, notifying all players via toast, without affecting player card marks.

## Why
Dispenser has no way to undo a mistakenly called number. Clicking a drawn number is currently a no-op.

## Where
- `openspec/changes/dispenser-unmark-number/proposal.md`
- Affected: `shared/types.ts`, `backend/src/game/GameRoom.ts`, `backend/src/game/handlers.ts`, `frontend/components/bingo-board.tsx`, `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx`

## Learned
- BingoBoard currently disables drawn numbers entirely — need to change to toggle semantics
- Player card marks are purely client-side — unmark event should NOT trigger card unmarking
- No confirmation dialog exists for drawing; unmark will follow same one-click pattern

observations.title: sdd/dispenser-unmark/spec
observations.content:
# Delta Spec: Dispenser Unmark Number

---

## Domain: number-unmark (NEW)

### Requirement: Unmark Drawn Number

The system SHALL allow the dispensador to remove a previously drawn number from the game's drawn set. When a number is unmarked, the system MUST broadcast a `numberUnmarked` event to all players in the game room, including the updated `drawnNumbers` array. The system MUST NOT automatically remove any marks from player cards.

#### Scenario: Dispenser unmarks a previously drawn number

- GIVEN a game in `playing` state with number 42 in `drawnNumbers`
- AND the client is the dispensador
- WHEN the client emits `unmarkNumber` with `{ gameId, number: 42 }`
- THEN the server removes 42 from `drawnNumbers`
- AND broadcasts `numberUnmarked` with `{ number: 42, drawnNumbers: [...] }` to all clients in the room

#### Scenario: Player card marks remain after unmark

- GIVEN number 42 was drawn and a player has manually marked cell 42 on their card
- WHEN the dispensador unmarks number 42
- THEN `numberUnmarked` is broadcast with the updated `drawnNumbers`
- AND the player's card `marked` array is NOT modified by the server or event payload

### Requirement: Unmark Validation

The system SHALL validate unmark requests. The server MUST reject unmark attempts when: (1) the number is not in `drawnNumbers`, (2) the client is not the dispensador, (3) the game status is not `playing`, (4) the number is out of range (not 1–90).

#### Scenario: Unmark a number that was never drawn

- GIVEN a game in `playing` state and number 42 is NOT in `drawnNumbers`
- WHEN the client emits `unmarkNumber` with `{ gameId, number: 42 }`
- THEN the server emits an `error` with `{ code: NUMBER_NOT_DRAWN, message: "Ese número no fue marcado" }`

#### Scenario: Non-dispensador attempts to unmark

- GIVEN a game in `playing` state and a player who is NOT the dispensador
- WHEN that player emits `unmarkNumber`
- THEN the server emits an `error` with `{ code: NOT_DISPENSADOR, message: "Solo el dispensador puede desmarcar números" }`

#### Scenario: Unmark in a finished game

- GIVEN a game with status `ended`
- WHEN the dispensador emits `unmarkNumber`
- THEN the server emits an `error` with `{ code: GAME_ENDED, message: "La partida ya terminó" }`

#### Scenario: Unmark with invalid number range

- GIVEN a game in `playing` state
- WHEN the dispensador emits `unmarkNumber` with number 0 or 91
- THEN the server emits an `error` with `{ code: NUMBER_NOT_DRAWN, message: "Número inválido (debe ser entre 1 y 90)" }`

### Requirement: Unmark Frontend — Dispenser Toggle

The BingoBoard component MUST treat drawn numbers as clickable (not disabled). When the dispensador clicks a drawn number, the client MUST emit `unmarkNumber`. When the dispensador clicks an undrawn number, the client MUST emit `drawNumber`. This replaces the previous draw-only behavior.

#### Scenario: Dispenser clicks a drawn number to unmark it

- GIVEN the dispensador is viewing the BingoBoard
- AND number 42 is drawn (visually marked on the board)
- WHEN the dispensador clicks number 42
- THEN the client emits `unmarkNumber` with `{ gameId, number: 42 }`

#### Scenario: Dispenser clicks an undrawn number to draw it

- GIVEN the dispensador is viewing the BingoBoard
- AND number 42 is NOT drawn
- WHEN the dispensador clicks number 42
- THEN the client emits `drawNumber` with `{ gameId, number: 42 }`

### Requirement: Unmark Frontend — Toast Notification

All clients (dispensador and players) MUST display a toast notification when they receive a `numberUnmarked` event. The toast MUST show which number was removed and auto-dismiss after a reasonable time (suggested: 5 seconds). The `drawnNumbers` array in local game state MUST be updated from the event payload.

#### Scenario: Player receives unmark toast notification

- GIVEN a player is connected to a game
- WHEN the player receives `numberUnmarked` with `{ number: 42, drawnNumbers: [...] }`
- THEN the player sees a toast: "Número 42 fue removido por el dispensador"
- AND the local `gameState.drawnNumbers` is updated to the received array
- AND the toast auto-dismisses after 5 seconds

#### Scenario: Dispenser receives unmark confirmation

- GIVEN the dispensador unmarked number 42
- WHEN the `numberUnmarked` event is received
- THEN the dispensador's `drawnNumbers` state updates
- AND the BingoBoard no longer shows 42 as drawn

---

## Domain: number-draw (MODIFIED)

### Requirement: Draw Number (modified)

(Current: `drawNumber` handler emits `numberDrawn` on valid draw and errors on already-drawn.)
(After: No change to draw behavior itself. Change is in the frontend — BingoBoard buttons for drawn numbers are no longer `disabled`, and `handleToggleNumber` dispatches draw OR unmark based on current state.)

(Previously: BingoBoard disabled drawn numbers; handleToggleNumber ignored already-drawn numbers.)

The system SHALL allow the dispensador to draw a number (1–90) that has not yet been drawn. The frontend BingoBoard MUST visually distinguish drawn vs undrawn numbers but MUST NOT disable drawn numbers. The frontend `handleToggleNumber` logic MUST check if the number is currently drawn: if drawn → emit `unmarkNumber`, if not drawn → emit `drawNumber`.

#### Scenario: Dispenser draws an undrawn number (unchanged)

- GIVEN a game in `playing` state with number 7 NOT in `drawnNumbers`
- AND the client is the dispensador
- WHEN the client emits `drawNumber` with `{ gameId, number: 7 }`
- THEN the server adds 7 to `drawnNumbers`
- AND broadcasts `numberDrawn` with `{ number: 7, drawnNumbers: [...] }`

#### Scenario: Draw a number already drawn (unchanged)

- GIVEN number 7 is already in `drawnNumbers`
- WHEN the dispensador emits `drawNumber` with number 7
- THEN the server emits error `{ code: NUMBER_ALREADY_DRAWN, message: "Ese número ya fue marcado" }`

#### Scenario: Drawn number is clickable on BingoBoard (NEW)

- GIVEN the dispensador is viewing the BingoBoard
- AND number 42 is drawn
- THEN number 42 is visually styled as drawn BUT is NOT disabled
- AND clicking number 42 dispatches `unmarkNumber` instead of being a no-op

---

## Event Schema

### Client → Server: `unmarkNumber`

```typescript
interface UnmarkNumberPayload {
  gameId: string;
  number: number; // 1–90
}
```

### Server → Client: `numberUnmarked`

```typescript
interface NumberUnmarkedPayload {
  number: number;
  drawnNumbers: number[]; // full updated array after removal
}
```

---

## Error Codes

| Code | Value | When |
|------|-------|------|
| `NUMBER_NOT_DRAWN` | `NUMERO_NO_MARCADO` | Number is not in `drawnNumbers` (cannot unmark what wasn't drawn) |
| `NOT_DISPENSADOR` | `NO_ERES_DISPENSADOR` | Non-dispensador attempts unmark |
| `GAME_ENDED` | `PARTIDA_TERMINADA` | Game status is `ended` |
| Out of range | `NUMERO_INVALIDO` (existing) | Number not in 1–90 range |

---

## Security / Rules

| Rule | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Only dispensador MAY unmark | The `unmarkNumber` handler MUST validate `socket.data.playerId === room.dispensadorId` |
| Game MUST be in `playing` state | Unmark in `waiting` or `ended` status returns `GAME_ENDED` or `GAME_NOT_FOUND` |
| Player marks are NOT removed | The `numberUnmarked` event carries no card data; client card `marked[]` arrays are untouched |
| No confirmation dialog | One-click toggle, consistent with existing draw behavior |
| drawnNumbers is the source of truth | The `drawnNumbers` array in the event payload is authoritative — clients MUST replace their local array, not patch it |

observations.title: sdd/En el proyecto actual del bingo, permitir que el jugador en sus cartones pueda desmarcar números manualmente./explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Permitir al jugador desmarcar números manualmente en sus cartones

### Current State

**Two independent marking systems exist**, and they work very differently:

**1. Dispensador global number board (server-authoritative):**
- The `GameRoom` holds `drawnNumbers: Set<number>` on the server — the source of truth for which numbers have been called.
- The dispensador clicks numbers on the `BingoBoard` component (10×9 grid, 1–90). `handleToggleNumber` emits `drawNumber` (if not drawn) or `unmarkNumber` (if already drawn). Both are broadcast to all players via `numberDrawn` / `numberUnmarked`.
- **The dispensador already CAN unmark numbers globally.** The `unmarkNumber` handler, `GameRoom.unmarkNumber()`, and `numberUnmarked` broadcast are all fully implemented and tested.

**2. Player card marking (purely client-side):**
- Each player's `Card.marked[]` array (27 booleans) lives EXCLUSIVELY in React state + `sessionStorage`. The server has ZERO knowledge of which cells a player has marked.
- The `BingoCard` component (`frontend/components/card.tsx`) renders each card as a 9-column × 3-row grid. The `canMark()` function determines clickability: `num > 0 && isDrawn(num) && !card.marked[cellIndex]`. A cell is only clickable if it has a number, that number has been drawn, AND it is NOT already marked.
- `handleMarkCard` in the game page performs an optimistic local update (`marked[cellIndex] = true`) and emits the `markCard` socket event. On the server, `markCard` handler only validates basic indices (0–26) and echoes back `cardMarked` to the same player — it does NOT store or validate anything about the card state.
- **There is NO mechanism for a player to unmark a cell.** Once marked, `canMark()` returns `false`, the button is `cursor-default`, and onClick does nothing.

**Key architectural insight:** The `markCard` event exists but is essentially a no-op path. It echoes back to the same player without any server-side mutation. Card state is ephemeral — if a player refreshes the page, they lose their marks (unless `sessionStorage` was updated, which it isn't for marks in the current code — only the initial cards and drawnNumbers are persisted).

**Line/Bingo detection** runs client-side via pure functions `hasLine()` and `hasBingo()` in the game page. They check `card.marked[]` against the card's numbers — they do NOT cross-reference with `drawnNumbers`. This means:
- If the dispensador globally unmarks a number that a player had already marked on their card, the player's card remains marked for that number. The player could still call line/bingo with an "orphaned" mark.
- This is an EXISTING design gap, not introduced by player-side unmarking.

### Affected Areas

- `frontend/components/card.tsx` (BingoCard component, lines 1–121) — **Primary change**: modify `canMark()` to allow unmarking; add visual unmark affordance on marked cells; modify onClick handler to support toggling.
- `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx` (GamePage, lines 1–630) — **Primary change**: `handleMarkCard` must toggle (mark/unmark) instead of only marking; may need a new handler `handleUnmarkCard`; must handle unmark-invalidated alerts (if a player unmarks a cell that was part of a line/bingo, the alert should disappear).
- `shared/types.ts` (lines 1–194) — **Optional**: add `UnmarkCardPayload` / `cardUnmarked` event types if we want a dedicated server event. Alternatively, overload `markCard` / `cardMarked` with an `action: 'mark' | 'unmark'` field.
- `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` (lines 316–342, markCard handler) — **Optional**: add server-side handling for unmark events if we introduce a new event. If we keep it client-only like current marking, no server changes needed.
- `backend/src/game/GameRoom.test.ts` (86 lines) — No changes needed (unmarkNumber on GameRoom already tested).
- `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` (151 lines) — **Optional**: add tests for new handler if introduced.
- `frontend/components/alerts.tsx` — **Minor**: may need to ensure alerts recalculate when a cell is unmarked (already handled by the `useEffect` that re-runs `detectAlert` on card changes).

### Approaches

**1. Client-only toggle (minimal change — RECOMMENDED)**
- Modify `BingoCard.canMark()` to also return `true` for already-marked cells (the purpose becomes "toggle mark" instead of just "mark").
- Modify `handleMarkCard` in the game page to detect if the cell is already marked: if yes, set `marked[cellIndex] = false` locally and emit a new `unmarkCard` event; if no, keep current behavior.
- Add a subtle visual cue on marked cells (e.g., slightly different radial gradient on hover, or a tiny "✕" on hover via CSS) to indicate they can be clicked to unmark.
- Handle `cardUnmarked` event on the server (or reuse `cardMarked` with a flag).
  - **Pros**: Minimal changes (2–3 files). Aligned with existing client-side architecture. No server state mutation needed. Low risk.
  - **Cons**: No server validation that the unmark is legitimate. Card state still ephemeral (lost on refresh). If the dispensador globally unmarks a number after a player marked it, the player's card still shows it as marked (existing gap, not new).
  - **Effort**: Low

**2. Client-only toggle with enhanced visual affordance**
- Same as Approach 1, but add a more explicit visual design for marked cells: a "wood chip" toggle button overlay that makes it obvious the chip can be picked up and placed back.
- Add a tooltip or brief instructional text: "Click para marcar, click de nuevo para desmarcar."
  - **Pros**: Better UX, very low risk. Same effort as Approach 1 plus design polish.
  - **Cons**: Slightly more CSS/design work. Same architectural limitations as Approach 1.
  - **Effort**: Low

**3. Server-tracked card state with sync**
- Move `card.marked[]` to the server (`Player.cards[].marked` in `GameRoom`).
- Add `markCard` and `unmarkCard` server handlers that mutate server state and broadcast `cardMarked`/`cardUnmarked` to all players.
- Player state survives refresh via server sync.
  - **Pros**: Consistent state, survives refresh, enables future features (spectator mode, game replay).
  - **Cons**: Major refactor (~400+ lines). More server memory per game (50 players × 5 cards × 27 booleans ≈ 7KB per game — negligible, but architectural complexity is the real cost). More network traffic. The current `markCard` handler becomes meaningful instead of a no-op.
  - **Effort**: High

### Recommendation

**Approach 2 (Client-only toggle with enhanced visual affordance)** is the right choice for this change. Here's why:

1. **Architecture alignment**: Card state is already client-side by design. The server is authoritative only for global game state (drawn numbers, game phase). Adding client-side unmarking is consistent with this architecture.
2. **The existing dispensador unmark confirms the pattern**: The codebase already has `unmarkNumber` / `numberUnmarked` for the 1–90 board. The pattern of "toggle mark state" is established.
3. **Line/Bingo alert recalculation works by default**: The `useEffect` in the game page re-runs `detectAlert()` whenever `cards` state changes — an unmark that invalidates a line/bingo will correctly dismiss the alert automatically. No extra logic needed.
4. **Risk is minimal**: The change is entirely in the frontend card component and game page handler. Server changes are optional (adding `cardUnmarked` event for consistency, but the current `markCard` handler pattern is a no-op anyway, so an unmark event would follow the same pattern).
5. **A full server refactor (Approach 3) is better addressed as a separate change** — it touches core architecture and affects the entire socket event contract. It should be justified by concrete requirements (e.g., reconnection resilience, spectator mode) rather than by the unmark feature alone.

### Risks

- **Orphaned marks on globally-unmarked numbers**: If the dispensador globally unmarks a number via `unmarkNumber`, players who had already marked that number on their cards will still see it marked. Their `hasLine`/`hasBingo` detection works on `card.marked[]`, not on `drawnNumbers`, so they could call line/bingo with an orphaned mark. This is an EXISTING gap (present before player unmarking), but player unmarking makes it slightly more relevant because players might WANT to unmark in response to a global unmark. Mitigation: this is a separate concern — automatically clearing player marks when a global number is unmarked. Should be tracked as a separate change.
- **Accidental unmark**: Players might unmark by mistake. Mitigation: the visual affordance (hover state, cursor change) makes the action intentional. The consequence is low — they can re-mark the cell.
- **Alert flickering**: If a player rapidly marks/unmarks a cell that completes a line, the alert modal could pop up and disappear repeatedly. Mitigation: the existing `lineAlertsSeen`/`bingoAlertsSeen` tracking prevents re-showing dismissed alerts. The 300ms React batching should also prevent intermediate renders in rapid clicks.
- **No test coverage for player mark/unmark**: `markCard` handler and `handleMarkCard` have zero tests. Mitigation: Add at least one test for the toggle logic (can be done in this change or noted as test debt).

### Ready for Proposal

**Yes.** The exploration is complete. The codebase already supports the dispensador unmarking numbers globally; the player card marking is purely client-side. Adding player-side unmark is a low-effort, low-risk change that follows existing patterns.

**What the orchestrator should tell the user**: The change is straightforward — the card component needs a toggle behavior for already-marked cells. We can proceed to the proposal phase. The key architectural decision is already made: keep card state client-side (consistent with current design). No server architecture changes needed. Estimated scope: 2–3 files, ~50-80 lines changed.
