observations.content:
# Proposal: Permitir al jugador desmarcar números manualmente en sus cartones

## Intent
El jugador actualmente puede marcar celdas en sus cartones pero no desmarcarlas. Necesitamos permitir que pueda corregir un error de marcado o desmarcar un número que ya no desea tener activo.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Modificar la lógica de marcado del cartón del jugador para permitir toggle (marcar/desmarcar).
- Agregar una señal visual en celdas marcadas que indiquen que se pueden desmarcar (hover/cursor).
- Emitir evento `unmarkCard` al servidor (siguiendo el patrón existente de `markCard`).
- Invalidar alertas de línea/bingo cuando un desmarcado rompe la combinación.
- Pruebas para la nueva lógica de toggle en el frontend.

### Out of Scope
- Migrar el estado de cartones al servidor (architectural refactor grande).
- Invalidación automática de marcas cuando el dispensador desmarca globalmente un número (gap existente, cambio separado).
- Cambios en el flujo de autorización del servidor para marcas (actualmente es no-op, se mantiene así).

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `player-card-unmark`: Permite al jugador desmarcar una celda previamente marcada en su cartón; emite evento `unmarkCard` y actualiza estado local.

### Modified Capabilities
- `player-card-mark`: El comportamiento de clic en celda pasa de "solo marcar" a "toggle mark/unmark". Se modifica `canMark()` y el handler `handleMarkCard`/`handleUnmarkCard`.

## Approach
Implementar un toggle client-side en el componente `BingoCard` y en el handler del game page. Las celdas marcadas mostrarán un estado hover que indique que se pueden desmarcar. El evento `unmarkCard` seguirá el patrón del existente `markCard` (echo de vuelta al mismo jugador sin mutación server-side). El sistema de alertas de línea/bingo ya recalcula automáticamente cuando cambia `card.marked[]`, por lo que no se requiere lógica adicional para invalidar alertas. Se mantiene la arquitectura client-side del estado de cartones.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `frontend/components/card.tsx` | Modified | `canMark()` permite toggle; agregar hover visual en celdas marcadas |
| `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx` | Modified | `handleMarkCard` soporta toggle; agregar `handleUnmarkCard`; emitir `unmarkCard` |
| `shared/types.ts` | Modified | Agregar `UnmarkCardPayload` y evento `cardUnmarked` |
| `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` | Modified | Agregar handler para `unmarkCard` (echo al mismo socket, mismo patrón que `markCard`) |
| `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` | Modified | Agregar tests para `unmarkCard` handler |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Desmarca accidental por parte del jugador | Med | Visual affordance (cursor pointer + hover state); el jugador puede volver a marcar inmediatamente |
| Alerta de línea/bingo parpadea al marcar/desmarcar rápido | Baja | `lineAlertsSeen`/`bingoAlertsSeen` evita re-mostrar alertas ya vistas |
| Marcas huérfanas al desmarcar globalmente un número (gap existente) | Alta (pre-existente) | Trackear como cambio separado; no en scope de este proposal |

## Rollback Plan
Revertir los commits que modifican `card.tsx`, `[gameId]/page.tsx`, `shared/types.ts` y `handlers.ts`. El estado de cartones es puramente client-side, por lo que no hay migración de datos necesaria.

## Dependencies
- Ninguna externa. Depende del evento socket.io-client ya configurado.

## Success Criteria
- [ ] El jugador puede hacer clic en una celda marcada y ésta se desmarca
- [ ] La celda desmarcada vuelve a ser marcable
- [ ] Las alertas de línea/bingo se actualizan automáticamente cuando un desmarcado rompe la combinación
- [ ] Existe una señal visual que indica que una celda marcada puede desmarcarse
- [ ] Tests cubren la lógica de toggle (mark/unmark) en el frontend o backend handler

observations.content:
# Delta for player-card-mark

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Toggle Cell Mark State

The player MUST be able to toggle the marked state of any cell on their card by clicking it.

(Previously: Player could only mark unmarked cells; marked cells were not clickable.)

#### Scenario: Mark an unmarked drawn number
- GIVEN a cell containing a drawn number that is not marked
- WHEN the player clicks the cell
- THEN the cell becomes marked
- AND the `markCard` event is emitted to the server

#### Scenario: Unmark a previously marked cell
- GIVEN a cell that is currently marked
- WHEN the player clicks the cell
- THEN the cell becomes unmarked
- AND the `unmarkCard` event is emitted to the server

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Visual Unmark Affordance

Marked cells SHOULD display a visual cue indicating they can be unmarked.

#### Scenario: Hover over marked cell
- GIVEN a marked cell
- WHEN the player hovers over it
- THEN the cursor becomes a pointer
- AND a subtle visual state change indicates the cell is toggleable

# Delta for player-card-unmark

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Unmark Event Protocol

The server MUST echo the `unmarkCard` event back to the emitting player after validating the payload.

#### Scenario: Server echoes unmark event
- GIVEN a player emits `unmarkCard` with valid card and cell indices
- WHEN the server receives the event
- THEN it validates the indices are within bounds (0–26)
- AND emits `cardUnmarked` back to the same socket

#### Scenario: Server rejects invalid unmark payload
- GIVEN a player emits `unmarkCard` with out-of-bounds indices
- WHEN the server receives the event
- THEN it MUST NOT emit `cardUnmarked`
- AND it MAY log the invalid request

### Requirement: Alert Recalculation on Unmark

The system MUST recalculate line and bingo alerts when a cell is unmarked.

#### Scenario: Unmark breaks a completed line
- GIVEN a card with a completed line where all cells are marked
- WHEN the player unmarks one cell in that line
- THEN the line alert is dismissed

#### Scenario: Unmark breaks bingo
- GIVEN a card with all required cells marked (bingo state)
- WHEN the player unmarks any cell
- THEN the bingo alert is dismissed

#### Scenario: Rapid mark/unmark does not re-show dismissed alert
- GIVEN a line alert has already been dismissed
- WHEN the player marks and unmarks cells in that line rapidly
- THEN the dismissed alert MUST NOT reappear

observations.content:
# Design: Permitir al jugador desmarcar números manualmente

## Technical Approach

Client-only toggle on card cells. `canMark()` becomes `canToggle()` — returning true for both marked and unmarked cells. `handleMarkCard` in the game page detects current mark state: emits `markCard` or `unmarkCard` accordingly. Server adds a mirror `unmarkCard` handler (echo back to emitting socket, same no-op pattern as existing `markCard`). Visual affordance: marked cells switch from `cursor-default` to `cursor-pointer` with a subtle hover brightness change. Alert recalculation works automatically via the existing `useEffect` dependency on `cards` state — no extra invalidation logic needed.

## Architecture Decisions

| Decision | Rejected | Chosen | Rationale |
|----------|----------|--------|-----------|
| Toggle API shape | Separate `onUnmark` prop on `BingoCard` | Single `onMark` callback; toggle detection in `handleMarkCard` | Keeps component API minimal. Toggle logic colocated in one handler. Matches dispensador's `handleToggleNumber` pattern. |
| Socket event contract | Overload `markCard`/`cardMarked` with `action: 'mark' \| 'unmark'` | Separate `unmarkCard`/`cardUnmarked` events | Follows existing dispensador pattern (`drawNumber`/`unmarkNumber` are distinct). Existing `cardMarked` listener only sets `marked[i]=true` — modifying it risks accidental unmark on reconnect replay. |
| Server handler scope | Client-only (no server change) | Server validates + echoes (mirror of `markCard`) | Consistent with existing `markCard` handler. Validates cardIndex≥0, cellIndex 0–26. Echo to emitting socket only. |
| Visual affordance | Text label ("click para desmarcar") | Cursor-pointer + `hover:brightness-110` on marked cells | Minimal visual noise. Cursor change is established web convention. Existing wood-chip radial gradient already distinguishes marked state clearly. |
| Alert invalidation | Explicit alert dismissal on unmark | Let existing `useEffect`/`detectAlert` recalculate automatically | `detectAlert()` already re-runs on every `cards` state change (page.tsx line 307). `lineAlertsSeen`/`bingoAlertsSeen` prevents re-showing dismissed alerts. Zero new code needed. |
| Server state migration | Move `card.marked[]` to server | Keep card state client-side | Out of scope per proposal. Consistent with current architecture where server is authoritative only for global game state. |

## Data Flow

```
Player clicks cell (marked or unmarked)
      │
      ▼
canToggle(cellIndex) → true (if num>0 AND isDrawn AND game not ended)
      │
      ▼
handleMarkCard(cardIndex, cellIndex) — checks card.marked[cellIndex]
      │
      ├─ currently MARKED → optimistic: marked[cellIndex]=false
      │                   → emit('unmarkCard', {gameId, cardIndex, cellIndex})
      │
      └─ NOT marked      → optimistic: marked[cellIndex]=true
                          → emit('markCard', {gameId, cardIndex, cellIndex})
      │
      ▼
setCards(...) → React re-render
      │
      ├─ BingoCard: marked cells now show cursor-pointer + hover brightness
      └─ useEffect([cards]): detectAlert() recalculates
           → dismisses alert if combination broken
           → (no re-show if alert already seen via lineAlertsSeen/bingoAlertsSeen)
      │
      ▼
Server: validates cardIndex≥0 && cellIndex in [0,26]
      → echoes cardMarked/cardUnmarked to emitting socket only
      → Client listener: idempotent state update (already applied optimistically)
```

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `frontend/components/card.tsx` | Modify | L27-31: `canMark()` → `canToggle()` — allow clicked on marked cells. L75: marked cells get `cursor-pointer hover:brightness-110` instead of `cursor-default`. L64: onClick fires for marked cells too. |
| `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx` | Modify | L345-364: `handleMarkCard` detects current mark state; toggles. If marked → emit `unmarkCard`. L200-212 area: add `cardUnmarked` event listener (sets `marked[cellIndex]=false`). |
| `shared/types.ts` | Modify | Add `UnmarkCardPayload` (`gameId, cardIndex, cellIndex`). Add `CardUnmarkedPayload` (`cardIndex, cellIndex`). Wire into `ClientToServerEvents` (`unmarkCard`) and `ServerToClientEvents` (`cardUnmarked`). |
| `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` | Modify | After L342: add `unmarkCard` handler. Validate cardIndex≥0, cellIndex 0–26. Echo `cardUnmarked` to emitting socket. Same no-op pattern as `markCard`. |
| `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` | Modify | Add `unmarkCard` handler tests: valid payload echoes `cardUnmarked`, out-of-bounds indices emit error. Follow existing mock pattern (L10-62). |

## Interfaces / Contracts

```typescript
// shared/types.ts — ADDITIONS

export interface UnmarkCardPayload {
  gameId: string;
  cardIndex: number;
  cellIndex: number;
}

export interface CardUnmarkedPayload {
  cardIndex: number;
  cellIndex: number;
}

// ClientToServerEvents — ADD
unmarkCard: (payload: UnmarkCardPayload) => void;

// ServerToClientEvents — ADD
cardUnmarked: (payload: CardUnmarkedPayload) => void;
```

`CardUnmarkedPayload` reuses the same shape as the existing `CardMarkedPayload`. Both have `{ cardIndex, cellIndex }`. Keep them separate types for clarity and future extensibility.

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| Unit (backend) | `unmarkCard` handler: valid indices echo `cardUnmarked` to socket; out-of-bounds (cellIndex<0, ≥27, cardIndex<0) rejected with error | Vitest. Two tests following `handlers.test.ts` mock pattern (mockIo, mockSocket, trigger). |
| Unit (frontend) | N/A | No frontend test infra exists. Toggle is a simple state flip — verified by backend unit coverage + manual smoke test. |

## Migration / Rollout

No migration required. Card state remains client-side (React state + sessionStorage). Rollback: revert the 5 files. No data migration, feature flags, or phased rollout needed.

## Open Questions

None. All design decisions are resolved by following existing architecture patterns.

observations.title: Implemented cell unmark toggle for bingo cards
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented player unmark toggle feature — cells can be clicked to unmark, server echoes unmarkCard event, visual affordance on marked cells.
**Why**: Player requested ability to manually unmark numbers on their bingo cards. Previously only marking was possible.

**What**: Arreglé la lógica de `canToggle` en `frontend/components/card.tsx` para permitir desmarcar celdas ya marcadas incluso si el dispensador quitó esa bola del tablero global.

observations.title: sdd/fix/cross-game-broadcast-security/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Cross-Game Broadcast Security Bug

### Current State

The backend Socket.io handlers in `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` associate a socket to a game via two mechanisms:
1. **Room membership**: `socket.join(gameId)` (line 66, 127) — socket joins the Socket.io room named after the gameId.
2. **Data storage**: `socket.data.gameId` and `socket.data.playerId` (lines 69-70, 130-131) — stored on the socket object for subsequent validation.

The helper `getGameForSocket()` (lines 440-463) reads `socket.data.gameId`, looks up the GameRoom from GameManager, and returns it — correctly validating that the socket belongs to SOME game.

**THE BUG**: After passing `getGameForSocket()`, event handlers use `payload.gameId` (untrusted client input) instead of `room.id` (the validated game ID) for their broadcast calls via `io.to(payload.gameId).emit(...)`. The server NEVER checks that `payload.gameId === socket.data.gameId`.

### Attack Flow

1. Malicious player connects to game "abc123" (socket.data.gameId = "abc123")
2. Victim players are in game "xyz789"
3. Attacker emits `drawNumber` with `{ gameId: "xyz789", number: 42 }`
4. `getGameForSocket` validates: socket.data.gameId = "abc123" → finds room → PASSES
5. `room.drawNumber(42)` mutates the CORRECT room (abc123)
6. `io.to("xyz789").emit('numberDrawn', ...)` broadcasts fake event to VICTIM room (xyz789)
7. Victims see a number drawn that never happened in their game

### Affected Areas

- `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` — 6 vulnerable event handlers (see below)

### Vulnerability Map — All Socket Event Handlers

| # | Event | Line | Uses `payload.gameId` for broadcast | Severity |
|---|-------|------|-------------------------------------|----------|
| 1 | `drawNumber` | 195 | `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('numberDrawn', ...)` | **HIGH** — injects fake numbers into victim games |
| 2 | `unmarkNumber` | 246 | `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('numberUnmarked', ...)` | **HIGH** — injects fake unmark into victim games |
| 3 | `toggleLine` | 277 | `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('lineToggled', ...)` | **MEDIUM** — injects line toggle alerts |
| 4 | `toggleBingo` | 305, 310 | `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('bingoToggled', ...)` + `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('gameEnded', ...)` | **CRITICAL** — can end another game, show fake winner |
| 5 | `callLine` | 390 | `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('lineToggled', ...)` | **MEDIUM** — injects line alerts |
| 6 | `callBingo` | 416-417 | `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('bingoToggled', ...)` + `io.to(payload.gameId).emit('gameEnded', ...)` | **CRITICAL** — can end another game, declare fake winner |

#### Events NOT vulnerable

| Event | Line | Why safe |
|-------|------|----------|
| `markCard` | 340 | Only calls `socket.emit()` (echo to sender only) |
| `unmarkCard` | 367 | Only calls `socket.emit()` (echo to sender only) |
| `createGame` | N/A | No broadcast, only `socket.emit()` to creator |
| `joinGame` | 141 | Broadcast uses `payload.gameId` but at this point the socket JUST joined that game — no cross-game risk since socket has no prior gameId |

### Socket Association Mechanism

Two fields are set on `socket.data`:
- **During `createGame`** (line 69-70): `socket.data.gameId = result.gameId`, `socket.data.playerId = result.playerId`
- **During `joinGame`** (line 130-131): `socket.data.gameId = payload.gameId`, `socket.data.playerId = result.player.id`

The helper `getGameForSocket(socket, gameManager)` (line 440):
1. Reads `socket.data.gameId`
2. If missing → emits error, returns null
3. Looks up room via `gameManager.getGame(gameId)`
4. If not found → emits error, returns null
5. Returns the GameRoom

**Key observation**: `getGameForSocket` correctly validates the socket's game, but then the handler discards the validated `room.id` and uses `payload.gameId` for broadcasting.

### Approaches

1. **Use `room.id` for all broadcasts (RECOMMENDED)**
   - Replace all `io.to(payload.gameId)` with `io.to(room.id)` in the 6 vulnerable handlers.
   - Since `room` is already obtained from `getGameForSocket` and `room.id` equals `socket.data.gameId` (guaranteed by GameManager lookup), this eliminates the untrusted input from the broadcast path.
   - Pros: Minimal change (6 lines), no new validation logic, leverages already-validated room object.
   - Cons: None.
   - Effort: **Low** (5 minutes of editing, test verification).

2. **Explicit validation: reject if `payload.gameId !== socket.data.gameId`**
   - Add a guard at the top of each handler: `if (payload.gameId !== socket.data.gameId) { emit error; return; }`
   - Pros: Explicit, easy to understand, catches malicious intent earlier.
   - Cons: Requires adding guard to each handler (~2 lines each), payload.gameId becomes dead parameter.
   - Effort: **Low-Medium** (more lines, but same net effect).

3. **Socket.io middleware to validate gameId on all events**
   - Use `io.use((socket, next) => ...)` to intercept ALL events and validate `payload.gameId` globally.
   - Pros: Centralized, catches future vulnerabilities automatically.
   - Cons: Socket.io middleware applies to connection/authentication, not to individual event payloads. Would need to use `socket.use(([event, ...args], next) => ...)` interceptor which is less common and could break typed event signatures. More complex.
   - Effort: **Medium** (Socket.io interceptor pattern, type safety concerns).

### Recommendation

**Approach 1: Replace `io.to(payload.gameId)` with `io.to(room.id)`.**

This is the minimal, surgical fix. It eliminates the root cause without adding complexity:
- The `room` object is already retrieved and validated by `getGameForSocket()`
- `room.id` is guaranteed to match `socket.data.gameId`
- No new error paths or validation logic needed
- 6 line changes total across the 6 affected handlers

After the fix, `payload.gameId` becomes unused in these handlers. Consider removing `gameId` from the payload types (`DrawNumberPayload`, `UnmarkNumberPayload`, `ToggleLinePayload`, `ToggleBingoPayload`, `CallLinePayload`, `CallBingoPayload`) in a follow-up cleanup — but that would require updating the frontend emit calls too. For the immediate fix, just changing the broadcast target is sufficient and safe.

### Risks

- **Low risk**: The frontend always sends the correct `gameId` (extracted from URL params in `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx` line 89), so removing the dependency on `payload.gameId` for broadcasts won't break legitimate clients.
- **Socket reconnection edge case**: If a socket reconnects, `socket.data` might be lost/reset. The current code already has no reconnection handler to restore `socket.data.gameId` — but this is a separate issue, not related to the cross-game bug. If reconnection happens, `getGameForSocket` would fail cleanly (emit "No estás en ninguna partida"), which is acceptable.
- **Type changes risk**: If we remove `gameId` from payload types, we must update the shared types AND the frontend emit calls. Recommendation: defer type cleanup to a follow-up PR; the immediate fix should not change types.

### Existing Tests

- `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` (265 lines) — Tests exist for `unmarkNumber` and `unmarkCard` handlers only. Tests use `mockIo.to` to verify broadcast targets. The `unmarkNumber` test passes `{ gameId: 'test01', number: 42 }` where `test01` matches `socket.data.gameId` — so existing tests don't detect the bug (payload.gameId happens to match the socket's gameId).
- `backend/src/game/GameRoom.test.ts` (86 lines) — Tests `unmarkNumber`, `drawNumber`, etc. Unit tests for GameRoom domain logic. Unaffected by this bug.
- `backend/src/game/CardGenerator.test.ts` — Card generation tests. Unaffected.
- **No integration/E2E tests** — The project has no Socket.io integration tests that could have caught this cross-game injection.

### Ready for Proposal

**Yes**. The exploration is complete. Recommend proceeding to `sdd-propose` with the following scope:
- Fix 6 broadcast calls in `backend/src/game/handlers.ts`
- Add test cases proving cross-game injection is blocked
- Do NOT change shared types (defer to cleanup PR)

observations.title: sdd/fix/cross-game-broadcast-security/proposal
observations.content:
## Proposal: Cross-Game Broadcast Security Bug Fix

## Intent

Fix a security vulnerability where a client can broadcast Socket.io events to arbitrary games by sending a mismatched `gameId` in the payload. The backend validates the socket's game membership via `getGameForSocket()`, but then broadcasts using the untrusted `payload.gameId` instead of the validated `room.id`, allowing cross-game event injection (fake number draws, bingo declarations, game endings).

## Scope

### In Scope
- Replace `io.to(payload.gameId)` with `io.to(room.id)` in 6 event handlers in `backend/src/game/handlers.ts`
- Add unit tests proving cross-game injection is blocked (mismatched payload.gameId cannot affect another game's room)

### Out of Scope
- Frontend changes
- API contract / payload type changes
- Shared type cleanup (removing `gameId` from payload types)
- Reconnection handling improvements

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- None

### Modified Capabilities
- None (pure implementation fix, no spec-level behavior changes)

## Approach

Surgical fix: in each of the 6 vulnerable handlers, change the broadcast target from `io.to(payload.gameId)` to `io.to(room.id)`. The `room` object is already retrieved and validated by `getGameForSocket()`; `room.id` is guaranteed to match the socket's actual game. This eliminates the untrusted payload from the broadcast path with zero new validation logic.

After the fix, add test cases to `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` that verify: a socket in game A emitting an event with `payload.gameId = "gameB"` does NOT result in any broadcast to game B's room.

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|------|--------|-------------|
| `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` | Modified | 6 broadcast calls switched from `payload.gameId` to `room.id` |
| `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` | Modified | New test cases for cross-game injection rejection |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|------|------------|------------|
| Frontend depends on payload.gameId for something else | Very Low | Confirmed: frontend only uses payload.gameId for emission; broadcast targets are server-side only |
| Existing tests break due to mock expectations | Low | Tests already mock `io.to()`; updating assertions is trivial |

## Rollback Plan

Revert the 6 line changes in `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` and remove the new test cases. No database migrations or frontend deployments involved — safe single-commit revert.

## Dependencies

- None

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 6 vulnerable event handlers (`drawNumber`, `unmarkNumber`, `toggleLine`, `toggleBingo`, `callLine`, `callBingo`) broadcast exclusively to `room.id`
- [ ] Unit tests confirm that a socket in game A cannot inject events into game B via manipulated `payload.gameId`
- [ ] Existing tests continue to pass
- [ ] No frontend or API contract changes

observations.title: sdd/fix/cross-game-broadcast-security/spec
observations.content:
# Spec: Cross-Game Broadcast Security Bug Fix

## Requirements

### R1: Validated Broadcast Target
Each of the 6 vulnerable Socket.io event handlers MUST broadcast exclusively to the socket's assigned game room (`room.id`), which is already validated by `getGameForSocket()`. The system MUST NOT use `payload.gameId` as a broadcast target.

Affected events: `drawNumber`, `unmarkNumber`, `toggleLine`, `toggleBingo`, `callLine`, `callBingo`.

### R2: Cross-Game Injection Immunity
A socket joined to game A that emits an event with `payload.gameId = "gameB"` SHALL NOT cause any broadcast to game B's room, and SHALL NOT mutate game B's state.

### R3: Backward Compatibility
For normal (matching) payloads where `payload.gameId === room.id`, existing functionality MUST remain unchanged.

### R4: Test Coverage
The test suite MUST contain cross-game injection tests for all 6 affected events, proving that a mismatched `gameId` in the payload cannot affect another game's room.

## Scenarios

### Scenario: drawNumber — Cross-Game Injection Blocked
- GIVEN socket S is in game A (room.id = "A")
- WHEN S emits `drawNumber` with `{ gameId: "B", number: 42 }`
- THEN `room.drawNumber(42)` is called on game A
- AND `io.to("A").emit('numberDrawn', ...)` is broadcast
- AND `io.to("B")` receives NO broadcast

### Scenario: unmarkNumber — Cross-Game Injection Blocked
- GIVEN socket S is in game A
- WHEN S emits `unmarkNumber` with `{ gameId: "B", number: 42 }`
- THEN `room.unmarkNumber(42)` is called on game A
- AND `io.to("A").emit('numberUnmarked', ...)` is broadcast
- AND `io.to("B")` receives NO broadcast

### Scenario: toggleLine — Cross-Game Injection Blocked
- GIVEN socket S is in game A
- WHEN S emits `toggleLine` with `{ gameId: "B" }`
- THEN `room.toggleLine()` is called on game A
- AND `io.to("A").emit('lineToggled', ...)` is broadcast
- AND `io.to("B")` receives NO broadcast

### Scenario: toggleBingo — Cross-Game Injection Blocked
- GIVEN socket S is in game A
- WHEN S emits `toggleBingo` with `{ gameId: "B" }`
- THEN `room.toggleBingo()` is called on game A
- AND `io.to("A").emit('bingoToggled', ...)` is broadcast
- AND if the game ends, `io.to("A").emit('gameEnded', ...)` is broadcast
- AND `io.to("B")` receives NO broadcast for either event

### Scenario: callLine — Cross-Game Injection Blocked
- GIVEN socket S is in game A
- WHEN S emits `callLine` with `{ gameId: "B" }`
- THEN `room.callLine()` is called on game A
- AND `io.to("A").emit('lineToggled', ...)` is broadcast
- AND `io.to("B")` receives NO broadcast

### Scenario: callBingo — Cross-Game Injection Blocked
- GIVEN socket S is in game A
- WHEN S emits `callBingo` with `{ gameId: "B" }`
- THEN `room.callBingo()` is called on game A
- AND `io.to("A").emit('bingoToggled', ...)` is broadcast
- AND if the game ends, `io.to("A").emit('gameEnded', ...)` is broadcast
- AND `io.to("B")` receives NO broadcast for either event

### Scenario: Normal Matching Payload Unchanged
- GIVEN socket S is in game A
- WHEN S emits any affected event with `{ gameId: "A", ... }`
- THEN the handler behaves exactly as before the fix

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All 6 vulnerable handlers use `io.to(room.id)` instead of `io.to(payload.gameId)`
- [ ] Cross-game injection tests exist for `drawNumber`, `unmarkNumber`, `toggleLine`, `toggleBingo`, `callLine`, `callBingo`

**What**: Fixed bug where the dispensador was always declared winner when toggleBingo was called, even if a player completed the bingo card.

**Why**: The toggleBingo handler hardcoded winner: dispensador?.name, breaking the game logic when a player won.

**Where**: 
- shared/types.ts — added winnerName?: string to ToggleBingoPayload
- backend/src/game/handlers.ts — uses payload.winnerName with fallback to dispensador
- backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts — added test for winnerName payload
- frontend/components/dispensador-controls.tsx — added player selector for winner
- frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx — passes players list and winnerName to toggleBingo

**Learned**: The game has two bingo paths: callBingo (player-declared) and toggleBingo (dispensador-confirmed). The latter was auto-assigning victory to the dispensador. Fix adds optional winnerName to toggleBingo so the dispensador can specify the real winner.

observations.title: Implemented server-side validation for callLine/callBingo
observations.content:
**What**: Implemented server-side validation so players cannot cheat by calling line or bingo without having a valid line/bingo on their cards given the drawn numbers.

**Why**: Previously, any player could call `callLine` or `callBingo` at any time without the server verifying whether their cards actually contained a line or bingo. This broke game integrity.

**Where**:
- `shared/bingo-logic.ts` (new) — pure functions `hasLine`, `hasBingo` (client-side, checking `card.marked[]`) and `hasLineServer`, `hasBingoServer` (server-side, checking against `drawnNumbers`)
- `shared/index.ts` — exports new bingo-logic functions
- `shared/types.ts` — added `LINE_NOT_COMPLETE` and `BINGO_NOT_COMPLETE` error codes
- `backend/src/game/handlers.ts` — `callLine` now validates with `hasLineServer` before broadcasting; `callBingo` validates with `hasBingoServer` before ending the game
- `backend/src/game/GameRoom.ts` — restored `unmarkNumber` method that was missing in main (needed by existing handlers)
- `frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx` — imports `hasLine`/`hasBingo` from `shared` instead of inline definitions
- `backend/src/game/bingo-logic.test.ts` (new) — 16 tests for all validation functions
- `backend/src/game/handlers.test.ts` — updated callLine/callBingo tests to use real players with valid cards; added 4 new validation tests

**Learned**:
- `hasLineServer` and `hasBingoServer` validate against `drawnNumbers` because the server does not track individual `card.marked[]` state (markCard/unmarkCard are client-side echoes)
- This prevents cheating while keeping the architecture simple
- All 67 backend tests pass; frontend builds successfully

observations.title: Restored dispensador unmark number clickability
observations.content:
**What**: Fixed BingoBoard component so the dispensador can click already-drawn numbers to unmark them.

**Why**: The button had `disabled={disabled || drawn}`, which disabled interaction when a number was already drawn. This prevented the dispensador from unmarking (toggling off) a previously drawn number.

**Where**: `frontend/components/bingo-board.tsx` — changed `disabled={disabled || drawn}` to `disabled={disabled}` and updated cursor styles so drawn numbers remain clickable.

**Learned**: The unmark feature was broken by a previous git checkout that reverted the worker's formatting changes but also reverted this functional fix.

observations.title: Docker dev workflow para bingo

**Why**: El usuario preguntó cómo operar cuando hace cambios y hay que hacer build.

- Hay 3 escenarios de cambios con Docker:
  1. Cambios en backend/frontend (.ts, .tsx): hot-reload automático, no se hace nada.
  2. Cambios en shared/: requiere recompilar `shared` (genera dist/) y reiniciar contenedores.
  3. Nuevas dependencias: requiere `npm install` en host + `docker compose build` + restart.
- Para solucionar el problema de shared, se monta `./shared/dist:/app/shared/dist` como volumen adicional en ambos servicios, de forma que el host puede compilar y los contenedores lo ven.

observations.title: Fix reconexión del jugador tras recarga
observations.content:
**What**: Implementé persistencia de estado en sessionStorage y auto-rejoin de sockets para que el jugador no pierda su progreso al recargar la página.
**Why**: El usuario reportó que al recargar el navegador del jugador con cartón, no se veían los números sorteados, ni las marcas, ni se podía marcar más.
**Where**:
- shared/types.ts — nuevos tipos RejoinGamePayload y GameRejoinedPayload
- backend/src/game/GameManager.ts — método rejoinGame()
- backend/src/game/handlers.ts — handler de socket rejoinGame
- frontend/app/game/[gameId]/page.tsx — persistencia en sessionStorage + auto-rejoin + handler gameRejoined
**Learned**:
- El problema tenía dos causas: (1) el estado del juego no se persistía en sessionStorage tras cada evento, y (2) el socket nuevo tras recarga no hacía join al room del juego, por lo que el servidor lo rechazaba como anónimo.
- La solución combinó: persistir drawnNumbers, cards, lineCalled, bingoCalled y status en cada evento relevante; y emitir rejoinGame automáticamente cuando el socket se reconecta, usando playerId guardado en sessionStorage.
- El backend ahora busca al jugador por playerId existente sin regenerar cartones, y reasocia el socket al room.
- El frontend prioriza los cartones del sessionStorage sobre los del servidor al rejoin, para conservar las marcas del usuario.

Hazme un plan para crear una nueva aplicación. La aplicación será un pequeño juego de bingo. Habrá dos tipos de jugadores, el dispensador que añade los números al juego, y los jugadores que tendrán uno o varios cartones de números para ir tachando. Cuando un usuario entra en la aplicación, verá las opciones de crear partida o añadirse a una. Una vez creada la partida, se generará un id para poder compartirolo con los otros jugadores para que se unan. El jugador que crea la partida al aceptar entra directamente a ella y le saldrá la opción de compartir id de la partida con los otros usuarios. Dentro ya de la partida, sólo un jugador puede ser dispensador y varios jugadores normales. Aparecerá una opción de elegir entre ser el dispensador, que sólo puede ser uno por partida, o jugador normal. Una vez en una partida ya hay un dispensador, otro jugador no puede serlo hasta terminar la partida. La vista del jugador dispensador será un tablero,como un bingo, con números del 1 al 90 que al pulsar encima se irán marcando, y si vuelve a pulsar encima se desmarcará. El dispensador tendrá un botón para marcar que se ha cantado línea y otro que se ha cantado bingo. Tanto el botón de línea como bingo se pueden activar y desactivar. Cuando un jugador normal marca para serlo, se le pedirá cuántos cartones quiere jugar, entre 1 y 5. Cada cartón contendrá 15 números elegidos al azar .El cartón conendrá 9 columnas por 3 filas. Cada columna corresponde a una decena, por ejemplo la primera del 1 al 9 y la última del 80 al 90. Cada fila contendrá en total 5 números . Cada columna se debe hacer para que haya entre 1 y 3 números elegidos al azar de la decena correspondiente.  A medida que el dispensador marca números, le aparecerán en la parte superior a los jugadores normales, los últimos 10 marcados. El usuario normal, sólo podrá marcar las casillas que contengan número. Si marca los 5 números de una línea, le saldrá una alerta de que cante línea, siempre que el dispensador no haya marc...

## Task: Implement server-side validation for `callLine` and `callBingo`

### Context
This is a multiplayer bingo game. Players join via Socket.io and receive bingo cards. Numbers are drawn by the dispensador and broadcast to all players. Players manually mark cells on their cards (client-side state echoed by server).

Currently, the server accepts `callLine` and `callBingo` events from any player without verifying whether the player's cards actually contain a valid line or bingo given the drawn numbers. This allows cheating.
